Applying \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel} to the matching conditions in \cref{def: construction des termes}, one can deduce $\sigma _{d} (\mathbf{u}^0_{p,\ell } )=\sigma _{d} (S^\infty_{p+d,\ell } )$ for~any $(p,\ell ,d)$. Moreover, \cref{construction directe des upl} gives
\begin{align*}
    \sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) &= \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) \\
    &= \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',0} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',0} ) \\
    &= \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \sum _{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}\\ p-p'=d'-d+2n}} \! c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',d'-d+2n,0} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell } )
\end{align*}
where we have used \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel} to establish the last two equalities. Let us rewrite the sum conditions on $p'$ w.r.t.\ $n$. $p'\in \mathbb{P}$ means $p-d'+d-2n\in \mathbb{P}$, $p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau$ means $d'-d-2\tau+2n \in \mathbb{P}$ (automatically satisfied), and $p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}$ means $p+d-2n\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}$, which is equivalent to $p+d-2n\in \mathbb{P}$. So, potentially adding a few vanishing terms, we deduce
\[\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )= \sum _{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}\\ 2n\leqslant p+d}} \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\leqslant p+d-2n}} \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d',n} )\cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p-d'+d-2n,\ell } ).\]
In particular, taking $\ell =0$, we obtain \cref{eq: simplification des sigma de CL cas irrationnel}. Moreover, by construction of the fields in \cref{def: construction des termes}, the established relations show that the families $((\mathbf{u}_{p,\ell } ,S_{p,\ell } ))_{p\in \mathbb{P}}$ are independent for different values of $\ell $. Only the family with $\ell =0$ has a non trivial initialization, namely $(\Delta +k_{0} ^2 )u_{0,0} =f_{\mathrm{s}}$. So it~is easy to deduce by induction that $\mathbf{u}_{p,\ell }$ and $S_{p,\ell }$ vanish for $p\in \mathbb{P}$ and $\ell >0$.

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us first treat $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ when $p-d<b$. By~\cref{expression de Rmacro phi avec les mcl}, we have
\begin{align*}
    c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } &:= \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) \\
    &= \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0} ^{b-1} \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \bigg) + \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=b} ^{\infty } \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \bigg) \\
    &= \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0} ^{b-1} \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \bigg) \quad\qquad  \mathrm{for} \ p-d<b
\end{align*}
since $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon$ send $\epsilon ^{n} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )[\ln \epsilon ]$ to $\epsilon ^{n+d} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )[\ln \epsilon ]$ for~any $n$. Moreover, the assumption $d'>-b$ yields $d'\not\in -b\mathbb{N}^*$. So \cref{expression sing heterog CL} states that, for~any $n<b$, $\Phi^0_{d',n}$ is a linear combination of the $\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{a}$ ($a\in \mathbb{R}$). Hence $\Phi^0_{d',n}$ does~not involve $\log (\alpha z)$. Using the same reasoning as in \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel} we deduce $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } = \delta _{d,d'} \,\delta _{p,d} \,\delta _{\ell ,0}$.
\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us treat $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ when $p+d'<b$. The proof of \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel} used that $\epsilon ^{d'} \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) = \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} )$. In the case $\tau \in \mathbb{Q}$, this equality does~not hold anymore but there~is still equality for some terms of these formal sums. Indeed, by \cref{Rmaicro defini et inversible dans Aemaicro,rq: def Eps}, $\epsilon ^{-d'} \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} )$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}^-_\epsilon(\Pi )$ and, by \cref{pb de Helmholtz dans Aemacro,action de Eps sur Helmholtz dans Aemaicro}, it~is solution of the Helmholtz problem \cref{eq: pb de Helmholtz dans Aemicro bis}. So \cref{pb de Helmholtz dans Aemicro} shows that we have
\[\epsilon ^{-d'} \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) = \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{p'\in \mathbb{P}} \,\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d''\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (p'+d'-\mathbb{P})}\, \sum _{\ell '\in \mathbb{N}} \sigma _{d'',p',\ell '} \big(\epsilon ^{-d'}  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} )\big) \cdot  \epsilon ^{p'\!} \,\ln ^{\ell '\!} \!\epsilon  \,\phi_{d''} \bigg)\]
so
\begin{subequations}
\label{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 1}
\begin{align}
    \epsilon ^{-d'} \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) &= \mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1} \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle \bigg(\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{p'\in \mathbb{P}} \,\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d''\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (p'+d'-\mathbb{P})}\, \sum _{\ell '\in \mathbb{N}} \,c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d'',d',p'+d',\ell '} \cdot  \epsilon ^{p'\!} \,\ln ^{\ell '\!} \!\epsilon  \,\phi_{d''} \bigg) \\
    &= \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{p'\in \mathbb{P}} \,\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d''\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (p'+d'-\mathbb{P})}\, \sum _{\ell '\in \mathbb{N}} \,c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d'',d',p'+d',\ell '} \cdot  \epsilon ^{p'\!} \,\ln ^{\ell '\!} \!\epsilon  \cdot \mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1} \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d''} )
    \label{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 1b} \\
    &= \mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1} \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d'} ) + \text{other terms} . 
    \label{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 1c}
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
As one can see in \cref{fig: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}, there~is a set of terms (the hatched zone) on which $\epsilon^{-d'}\langle\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle(\phi_{d'})$ and $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1}\circ\langle\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle(\phi_{d'})$ coincide, although they are~not globally equal (because of the other terms mentioned in \cref{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 1c}). We will see that, because of the assumption $p+d'<b$, $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ only ``sees'' the terms on which $\epsilon^{-d'}\langle\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle(\phi_{d'})$ and $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1}\circ\langle\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle(\phi_{d'})$ coincide. This will allow us to obtain for $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d'p,\ell }$ the same formula as in \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel}.

 
	\tikzset{external/export=true} 
	\tikzsetfigurename{fig-preuve_valeur_cmacro_cas_rationnel-} 
	\input{figures/preuve_valeur_cmacro_cas_rationnel.tex} 
	\tikzset{external/export=false} 
	\tikzsetfigurename{main-figure}

Applying $\sigma _{d,p,\ell }$ on both sides of \cref{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 1b} gives
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 2}}
    \delta _{d,d'} \,\delta _{p,-d'} \,\delta _{\ell ,0} = \sum _{p'\in \mathbb{P}} \,\sum _{d''\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (p'+d'-\mathbb{P})}\, \sum _{\ell '\in \mathbb{N}} \,c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d'',d',p'+d',\ell '} \cdot  c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} .
\end{equation}
For the left-hand side we used that $\sigma _{d} \circ R=0$ for~any $R\in \{R_{\Delta},R_{\mathrm{N}},R_{\partial_Y^2}\}$, which yields $\sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\epsilon ^{-d'} \phi_{d'} ) =\sigma _{d,p,\ell } (\epsilon ^{-d'} \phi_{d'} )$. As~for the right-hand side, it contains a finite number of non-zero terms by \cref{def: sigma et fsum commutent dans Aeps}. Let us precise what are these non-zero terms. Our final goal is to show that the right-hand side is equal to $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d',p,\ell }$.\\
Any $R\in \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}$ satisfies $\deg _{\epsilon } R\geqslant 0$ and $\deg _{\mathcal{A}} R\leqslant \deg _{\epsilon } R$, so we have
\[\langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d''} ) \in \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{p'\geqslant 0} \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{q\leqslant p'+d''} \epsilon ^{p'} \mathcal{A}_{q} (\Pi )[\ln \epsilon ] \qquad  \text{so}  \qquad  
\mathcal{H}_\epsilon^{-1} \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^-_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d''} ) \in \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{\substack{(p',q)\\ p'\geqslant -q, 0\leqslant p'+d''}} \epsilon ^{p'} \mathcal{A}_{q} (\Pi )[\ln \epsilon ].\]
Thus $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \neq 0$ only if $0\leqslant p-p'+d''$, which implies $p'+d'-d''<p+d'<b$ by assumption. Now using step~1, $p'+d'-d''<b$ yields $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d'',d',p'+d',\ell } =\delta _{d'',d'} \,\delta _{p'+d',d'} \,\delta _{\ell ',0}$. Therefore \cref{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 2} simplifies and becomes $\delta _{d,d'} \,\delta _{p,-d'} \,\delta _{\ell ,0} =c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d',p,\ell }$.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 3:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us treat $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ when $d<0$ and $p<b$. We recall its definition (for $d<0$):
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 3}}
    c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } := \! \sum _{\substack{(p_{1} ,p_{2} )\in (\mathbb{N}-d)\times (\mathbb{N}+d')\\ n\in \mathbb{N},\, p_{1} +p_{2} +2n=p}}
    \ \sum _{\substack{d_{1} \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p_{1} +d_{1} \in \mathbb{N}}} \ \sum _{\substack{d_{2} \in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p_{2} -d_{2} \in \mathbb{N}}}
    \ \sum _{\substack{(\ell _{1} ,\ell _{2} )\in \mathbb{N}^2 \\ \ell _{1} +\ell _{2} =\ell }}
    c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d_{1} ,p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }\cdot \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,n} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,d'\!,p_{2} ,\ell _{2} } .
\end{equation}
Let us show that any non-zero term satisfies $d_{1} >-b$, $p_{1} +d_{1} <b$ and $p_{2} -d_{2} <b$ in order to apply steps~1 and 2. We do it by contraposition, by showing that if a non-zero term verifies $d_{1} \leqslant -b$ or $p_{1} +d_{1} \geqslant b$ or $p_{2} -d_{2} \geqslant b$ then $p\geqslant b$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $d_{1} \leqslant -b$, then $p=p_{1} +p_{2} +2n=(p_{1} +d_{1} )-d_{1} +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n\geqslant 0+b+0+0+0=b$.
    \item Let us assume $p_{1} +d_{1} \geqslant b$. If $d_{1} >0$, then $\sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,n} ) =\delta _{d_{1} ,d_{2}} \delta _{n,0}$. Since we are looking at a non-zero term, we have $d_{1} =d_{2}$ and $n=0$. Thus $p=(p_{1} +d_{1} ) +(p_{2} -d_{2} ) \geqslant b+0$. Otherwise, we have $d_{1} <0$, which yields $p=(p_{1} +d_{1} )-d_{1} +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n \geqslant b+0+0+0+0=b$.
    \item If $p_{2} -d_{2} \geqslant b$, then $p=(p_{1} +d)-d +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n\geqslant 0+0+b+0+0=b$.
\end{itemize}
By~steps~1 and 2 we deduce that any non-zero term of \cref{eq: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel 3} satisfies $d=d_{1}$, $d_{2} =d'$, $p_{1} =-d$, $p_{2} =d$, $\ell _{1} =\ell _{2} =0$ and $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d_{1} ,p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }=c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,d'\!,p_{2} ,\ell _{2} }=1$. Similarly to \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel}, this implies the desired formula.
<!-- end demo-82 -->
<!-- demo-83: body_md -->
Let $p<b$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$. \Cref{construction directe des upl} states:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: preuve simplifications cas rationnel 1}}
    \sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) = \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) .
\end{equation}
The terms of this sum satisfy $p-p'\leqslant p<b$ and $d'\geqslant -p'>-p>-b$, so \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel} applies. Hence, similarly to \cref{simplifications cas irrationnel}, one can deduce 
\[{\textstyle \forall d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*}, \qquad  \sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )= \sum _{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}\\ 2n\leqslant p+d}} \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\leqslant p+d-2n}} \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d',n} )\cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p-d'+d-2n,\ell } ).\]
Taking $\ell =0$, it gives \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel}. In addition, like in \cref{simplifications cas rationnel}, it~is easy to deduce by induction that $u_{p,\ell } =0$ for~any $p<b$ and $\ell >0$. Moreover, for~any $p<2\tau$, the sums in the right-hand sides of \cref{eq: preuve simplifications cas rationnel 1,eq: simplifications cas rationnel} are empty, so \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel} and the property $(\ell >0 \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  u_{p,\ell } =0)$ can be extended to any $p<\max (b,2\tau)$. Finally, since $\tau = \frac{b}{a}$, we have $\max (b,2\tau)=p_{\min }$.
<!-- end demo-83 -->
<!-- demo-84: body_md -->
Let us prove points 1 and 2 only for $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}$ as it~is similar for $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}$. For~any $f \in \mathcal{A}(\Pi )$ s.t.\ $f _{|\Omega } = \Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} P(\log (\alpha z))]$ with $(q,k,P)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{N}\times \mathbb{R}[T]$, we have by~definition of $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon$
\[\mathcal{H}_\epsilon(f )_{|\Omega } = \sum _{j=0} ^{\deg P} \epsilon ^{d} \,\frac{\ln ^{j} \!\epsilon }{j!} \,\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} P^{(j)} (\log (\alpha z))]\]
So, for~any $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$, $\sigma _{d,p,0} \big(\mathcal{H}_\epsilon(f )\big) = \delta _{p,d} \,\sigma _{d} (f )=\sigma _{d,p-d,0} (f )$. Therefore, $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,0} := \sigma _{d,p,0} \circ \mathcal{H}_\epsilon\circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d'} ) = \sigma _{d,p-d,0} \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d'} )=\delta _{d,d'} \,\delta _{p,d}$, using that $\sigma _{d} \circ R=0$ for~any $R\in \{R_{\Delta},R_{\mathrm{N}},R_{\partial_Y^2}\}$.\\
Now let $\ell >0$ and $(d',p):=(d,d)$. The term of $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d} )$ in $\epsilon ^{d} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Pi )[\ln \epsilon ]$ is $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon(\phi_{d} ) =\epsilon ^{d} \phi_{d}$. Hence, $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } := \sigma _{d,d,\ell } \circ \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle (\phi_{d} ) =\sigma _{d,d,\ell } (\epsilon ^{d} \phi_{d} )=0$. Finally, if $(d',p) \neq (d,d)$ and $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$, then this coefficient depends on at least one variable among $k_{0}$, $k_{1}$ and $\frac{\mu _{0} }{\mu _{1}}$ by~definition of $\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}$.
<!-- end demo-84 -->
<!-- demo-85: body_md -->
Let us denote $\mathcal{P} :=(\mu _{0} ,\mu _{1} ,\rho _{0} ,\rho _{1} ,\omega )$ for simplicity.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let us assume that $w =c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ for some $(d,d',p,\ell )$. Then, by~definition of $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ and $\langle {\dots }\rangle $, we have\vspace{-1ex}
    \[w = \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) = \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \Bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0}^\infty \sum _{(R_{1} ,\dots ,R_{n} )\in \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}^{n}} R_{1} \circ \cdots \circ R_{n} (\phi_{d'} ) \Bigg).\]
    Moreover, by construction of $\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}$ in \cref{eq: def Rmaicro}, we have $\deg _{\mathcal{A}} R+2\deg _{\epsilon } R>0$ for any $R\in \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}$. Hence, there exists $n_{0}$ that depends only on $(d,d',p)$ and not on $\mathcal{P}$ s.t. 
    \[w = \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \Bigg( \sum _{n=0} ^{n_{0}} \sum _{(R_{1} ,\dots ,R_{n} )\in \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}^{n}} R_{1} \circ \cdots \circ R_{n} (\phi_{d'} ) \Bigg) .\]
    Now, given how $\@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}$ depends on $\mathcal{P}$, it~is easy to see that $F:\mathcal{P} \mapsto w$ is analytic. So, by properties of analytic functions, $F\neq 0$ iff $F$ is almost everywhere non-zero. This means that $w$ is not always zero iff it~is generically non-zero. Similarly, one can show this property if $w =c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d',p,\ell }$.
    \item If $w =c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$, then $w$ is an analytic function of some coefficients $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}$, $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}$ and some corner profile coefficients $(\sigma _{q_{1}} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d_{1} ,n_{1} }),\dots ,\sigma _{q_{I}} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d_{I} ,n_{I} })) =: \mathcal{Q}$. By~point 1, we deduce that $w$ is analytic in $(\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q})$ and the same property of analytic functions can be used to conclude.
    \item Finally, let us assume that $w$ is equal to some $\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )$ or $u^0_{p,\ell }$. Then, using \cref{def: genericite}, it~is easy to check by induction on $p$ that, if $w$ is~not generically non-zero, then $w$ is always zero.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end demo-85 -->
<!-- demo-86: body_md -->
\def\tau{\tau}                              
It suffices to consider $p\in \mathbb{P}$, as otherwise $u_{p,\ell } :=0$ by convention. Let us prove the property by induction on $p$. The case $p=0$ is obvious by \cref{def: genericite}. Let us prove the property for $p\in \mathbb{P} \setminus \{0\}$. Let $\tau:= \frac{\pi }{\Theta }$ and $E:=\mathbb{N}+(\mathbb{N} \setminus \{1\})\tau$.\\
First let us assume $p\in E$. There exist $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and $m\in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{1\}$ s.t.\ $p=n+m\tau$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $n\geqslant 1$, then the Dirichlet condition on $\Gamma $ of $u_{p,0}$ involves $u_{p-1,0}$, which is generically non-zero by $p-1\in E$ and induction hypothesis.
    \item Otherwise, $m\geqslant 2$. In this case, \cref{eq: def genericite : formule des CCL} with $d:=-\tau$ contains a term $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{-\tau,\tau,2\tau,0} \cdot \sigma _{\tau} (u_{p-2\tau,} 0)$. We know that $\sigma _{\tau} (u_{p-2\tau,0} )$ is generically non-zero by induction hypothesis because $p-2\tau \in E$. Hence it suffices to prove that $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{-\tau,\tau,2\tau,0}$ is generically non-zero to deduce that $\sigma _{-\tau} (u_{p,0} )$ and $u_{p,0}$ are generically non-zero. Let us compute this coefficient:
    \begin{align*}
        c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{-\tau,\tau,2\tau,0} &:= \! \sum _{\substack{(p_{1} ,p_{2} )\in (\mathbb{N}+\tau)\times (\mathbb{N}+\tau)\\ n\in \mathbb{N},\, p_{1} +p_{2} +2n=2\tau}}\ \sum _{\substack{d_{1} \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p_{1} +d_{1} \in \mathbb{N}}} \ \sum _{\substack{d_{2} \in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p_{2} -d_{2} \in \mathbb{N}}}	c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{-\tau,d_{1} ,p_{1} ,0}\cdot \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,n} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,\tau,p_{2} ,0} \\
        &= \sum _{\substack{d_{1} \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ \tau+d_{1} \in \mathbb{N}}} \ \sum _{\substack{d_{2} \in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ \tau-d_{2} \in \mathbb{N}}}	c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{-\tau,d_{1} ,\tau,0}\cdot \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,0} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,\tau,\tau,0} 
    \end{align*}
    because the condition in the first sum over $(p_{1} ,p_{2} ,n)$ implies $p_{1} =p_{2} =\tau$ and $n=0$. Then:
    \begin{alignjustif}[\quad]
        c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{-\tau,\tau,2\tau,0} &= \sum _{\substack{d_{1} \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ \tau+d_{1} \in \mathbb{N}}} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{-\tau,d_{1} ,\tau,0}\cdot \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{\tau,0} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{\tau,\tau,\tau,0} & \text{because }  d_{2} =\tau \\[5ex]
        &= c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{-\tau,-\tau,\tau,0}\cdot \sigma _{-\tau} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{\tau,0} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{\tau,\tau,\tau,0} + c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{-\tau,\tau,\tau,0}\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{\tau,\tau,\tau,0} & \text{because }  \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{\tau,0} ) =\delta _{d_{1} ,\tau} \text{ for }  d_{1} >0\\[1ex]
        &= \sigma _{-\tau} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{\tau,0} ) & \text{by \cref{classification coefs cmaicro}} 
    \end{alignjustif}
    So $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{-\tau,\tau,2\tau,0}$ is generically non-zero, which proves that $u_{p,0}$ is generically non-zero.
\end{itemize}
Conversely, let us show that, if there exists $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ s.t.\ $u_{p,\ell } \neq 0$, then $p\in E$. Without loss of generality, we can assume $p>0$. If $u_{p,\ell } \neq 0$, then either $u_{p,\ell |\Gamma } \neq 0$ or there exists $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$ s.t.\ $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) \neq 0$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item In the first case, since $u_{p,\ell |\Gamma }$ depends on the $u_{p-1-2n,\ell }$, there exists $n\in \mathbb{N}$ s.t.\ $u_{p-1-2n,\ell } \neq 0$. By~induction hypothesis, we have $p-1-2n\in E$, so $p\in E$.
    \item In the other case, there exist a term ``$c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} )$'' in \cref{eq: def genericite : formule des CCL} that does~not vanish. It satisfies $p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+2\tau$ and $u_{p',\ell '} \neq 0$, so $p'\in E$. Thus, $p=(p-p')+p'\in E$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end demo-86 -->
<!-- paragraphesansboite-10: body_md -->
To avoid too heavy formulas in the tables, we denote $\tau:=\tau$ in this section.
<!-- end paragraphesansboite-10 -->
<!-- demo-87: body_md -->
By~\crefrange{eq: def BesselY_a}{eq: BesselY pour n et -n} and the definition of $J_{a} ,\mathcal{J}_{a}$, $\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{a}$ in \crefrange{eq: def BesselJ}{eq: def BesselOmega}, the only non obvious case is $\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{n}$ when $n\in \mathbb{N}$. We need the following calculation: for~any $z\in \mathbb{C}$ with polar decomposition $re^{\mathrm{i}\theta }$, we have
\begin{multline*}
    \Im[(\alpha z)^{n+k} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log (\alpha z)] - \Im[(\alpha z)^{k} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{n+k} \log (\alpha z)] \\
    \begin{array}{l}
    = \Im[r^{n+2k} e^{\mathrm{i}n(\theta -\Theta )} (\ln r+\mathrm{i}(\theta -\Theta ))]- \Im[r^{n+2k} e^{-\mathrm{i}n(\theta -\Theta )} (\ln r+\mathrm{i}(\theta -\Theta ))] \\[\jot]
    = \Im[r^{n+2k} e^{\mathrm{i}n(\theta -\Theta )} (\ln r+\cancel{\mathrm{i}(\theta -\Theta )})]+ \Im[r^{n+2k} e^{\mathrm{i}n(\theta -\Theta )} (\ln r-\cancel{\mathrm{i}(\theta -\Theta )})] \\[\jot]
    = 2\, r^{n+2k} \sin (n(\theta -\Theta )) \ln r 
    \end{array}
\end{multline*}
This shows the second sum in \cref{eq: def BesselYOmega_n} converges to
$\frac{2}{\pi } J_{n} (k_{0} r) \ln (k_{0} r/2) \sin (n(\theta -\Theta ))$. Therefore we have $\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{n} \longrightarrow  Y_{n} (k_{0} r) \sin (n(\theta -\Theta ))$.
<!-- end demo-87 -->
<!-- demo-88: body_md -->
The properties of $J_{a}$ that are used in the proof of \cref{relations sur BesselGamma/Omega}, e.g.\ $2 J_{a} '(z) = J_{a-1} (z)-J_{a+1} (z)$, also hold for $Y_{a}$ by \cite{Leb72}. Hence points 1 to 4 hold for $x\mapsto Y_{a} (k_{0} x)$ and $(r,\theta ) \mapsto  Y_{a} (k_{0} r) \sin (a(\theta -\Theta ))$. It remains to show that this implies the same relations on the formal series $\mathcal{Y}_{a}$ and $\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{a}$, i.e.\ term by term.\smallskip\par
For~any $a\in \mathbb{R}$, there exist $(d_{n} )\in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ and $(c_{n} ),(c'_{n} ) \in \mathbb{C}^{\mathbb{N}}$ s.t.\ $d_{n} \rightarrow \infty $ and
\[\forall x>0, \qquad  Y_{a} (k_{0} x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty  x^{d_{n}} (c_{n} + c'_{n} \ln x).\]
In addition we have $c_{n} =O(\rho ^{d_{n}} )$ and $c'_{n} =O(\rho ^{d_{n}} )$ for~any $\rho >0$ (using $\psi (k)=O(\ln k)$ when $k\rightarrow \infty $). One can verify that this implies
\[\forall j\in \mathbb{N},\forall q\in \mathbb{R}, \qquad  \partial _{x} ^{j} \big[Y_{a} (k_{0} x)\big] = \sum _{n\in \mathbb{N},\. d_{n} \leqslant q} \partial _{x} ^{j} \big(x^{d_{n}} (c_{n} + c'_{n} \ln x)\big) + o(x^{q-j} ).\]
Hence we deduce:
\[\forall q\in \mathbb{R}, \qquad  Y_{a} (k_{0} x) = T_{\leqslant q} (\mathcal{Y}_{a} ) + o_{\partial } (x^{q} ) \quad  \text{ and } \quad  Y_{a} (k_{0} r) \sin (a(\theta -\Theta )) = T_{\leqslant q} (\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{a} ) + o_{\partial } (r^{q} ).\]
Using \cref{derivation des DA dans Amaicro}, we obtain
\[\forall q\in \mathbb{R}, \qquad  0 = (\Delta +k_{0} ^2 )\big[Y_{a} (k_{0} r) \sin (a(\theta -\Theta )) \big] = T_{\leqslant q} \circ (\Delta +k_{0} ^2 )(\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{a} ) + o_{\partial } (r^{q} ).\]
By~uniqueness of the asymptotic expansion in $\mathcal{A}^+\hspace{-0.15ex}$ (see \cref{unicité du DA}), this yields $(\Delta +k_{0} ^2 )(\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{a} ) = 0$. Similarly for the other relations.
<!-- end demo-88 -->
<!-- demo-89: body_md -->
Similarly to \cref{sigma de BesselOmega}, one can verify that each function of the form $\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log (\alpha z)^{j} ]$ that appears in \cref{eq: def BesselYOmega_n} either vanishes or belongs to the basis of $\mathcal{A}(\Omega )$ used to define $\sigma _{d}$ in \cref{def: sigma}. Thus the values of $\sigma _{d} (\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{n} )$ (for $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}* \setminus \{-n,n\}$) and $\sigma _{-n} (\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{n} )$ (when $n\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$) follow easily, and we have (when $n\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$)
\[\sigma _{n} (\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{n} ) = \frac{2}{\pi \.\Gamma (n+1)} \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{n} \ln \!\left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right) - \frac{\psi (1)+\psi (n+1)}{\pi \.n!} \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{n} = \frac{2\ln (k_{0} /2)-H_{n} +2\gamma }{\pi \.n!} \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{n} \]
because $\Gamma (n+1)=n!$ and $\psi (m)=H_{m-1} -\gamma $ for~any $m\in \mathbb{N}^*$ (see \cite{Leb72}).
<!-- end demo-89 -->
<!-- demo-90: body_md -->
\def\mathcal{Z}{\mathcal{Z}} 
\def\mathcal{Z}^\Omega{\mathcal{Z}^\Omega} 
\def\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}{\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}} 
The reasoning in the proof of \cref{expression sing homog CL} shows the following result.
\begin{quote}
    ``Let $(\mathcal{Z}_{a} )\in \mathcal{A}^+\hspace{-0.15ex}(\Gamma )^{\mathbb{R}}$ and $(\mathcal{Z}^\Omega_{a} )\in \mathcal{A}^+\hspace{-0.15ex}(\Omega )^{\mathbb{R}}$ be two families. We assume that they satisfy the relations of \cref{relations sur BesselGamma/Omega,relations sur BesselYGamma/Omega} (which are the same) and that we have: $\forall d\in \mathbb{R} \setminus \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*,\,\allowbreak \forall q\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*,\; \sigma _{q} (\mathcal{Z}^\Omega_{d} )=0$. For~any $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$, let us denote
    \[\forall n\in -\mathbb{N}^*,\ \ \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n} :=0 \qquad  \text{ and } \qquad  \forall n\in \mathbb{N},\quad  \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n} := \sum _{m=-n} ^{n} a_{n,m} \mathcal{Z}^\Omega_{d+m} .\]
    Then for any $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$ and $n\in [\![1,b-1]\!]$, $\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n}$ is the unique solution in $\mathcal{A}^+\hspace{-0.15ex}(\Omega )$ of 
    \[ \left\{\begin{array}{r@{\;=\;}ll}
        (\Delta +k_{0} ^2 )\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n} & 0 &\text{ in }\Omega  \\
        \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n} & \sum\limits_{m=0}^\infty  \frac{\mu _{0} }{\mu _{1}} \,T_{m} \cdot  (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )^{m} \partial _{y} \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n-1-2m} &\text{ on }\Gamma  \\
        \sigma _{q} (\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{d,n} ) & 0 &\ \forall q\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\, \text{''} 
        \end{array}\right.\]
\end{quote}
\Cref{expression sing homog CL} applies this principle to $(\mathcal{Z}_{a} ):=(\mathcal{J}_{a} )$ and $(\mathcal{Z}^\Omega_{a} ):=(\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{a} )$. Thanks to \cref{relations sur BesselYGamma/Omega}, \ref{sigma de BesselYOmega} and \ref{sigma de BesselOmega}, it can also be applied to $(\mathcal{Z}_{a} ):=(\mathcal{Y}_{a} )$ and $(\mathcal{Z}^\Omega_{a} ):=(\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{a} )$. Given \cref{expression sing homog CL avec BesselY}, this gives the desired result.
<!-- end demo-90 -->
<!-- demo-91: body_md -->
\def\mu_{\rm r}{\mu_{\rm r}} 
\defk_{\rm r}{k_{\rm r}} 
\deft_{#}1{t_{#1}} 
We only prove the case $d\not\in -\mathbb{N}$, but the result can be extended to the case $d\in -\mathbb{N}$ using the same method as \cref{expression sing heterog CL avec BesselY}. We take the notations of \cref{ex: expression sing heterog CL}: $\mu_{\rm r}:= \frac{\mu _{0} }{\mu _{1}}$, $k_{\rm r} := \big( \frac{2k_{1} }{k_{0}} \big)^2 $ and $t_{m} :=\operatorname{cotan}(m\Theta )$ for~any $m\in \mathbb{N}$. We also denote $\eta  :=(-1)^{d\Theta /\pi }$. Similarly to \cref{ex: expression sing heterog CL}, one can show that the following formulas of $\Phi^0_{d,n|\Gamma }$ hold when $n\leqslant b$ (this is actually an intermediate step to obtain the formulas of \cref{ex: expression sing heterog CL}):
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\displaystyle \Phi^0_{d,1|\Gamma } = \eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{1-d} \mu_{\rm r} \.(\mathcal{J}_{d-1} + \mathcal{J}_{d+1} )$
    \item $\displaystyle \Phi^0_{d,2|\Gamma } = \eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{2-d} \mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1} \.(\mathcal{J}_{d-2} - \mathcal{J}_{d+2} )$
    \item $\displaystyle \Phi^0_{d,3|\Gamma } = \eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{3-d} \bigg[ \frac{3\mu_{\rm r}^{3} t_{1}t_{2} + \mu_{\rm r}}{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-3} + \mathcal{J}_{d+3} )
    + \frac{3\mu_{\rm r}^{3} t_{1}t_{2} +\mu_{\rm r}(k_{\rm r}-1)}{3}  (\mathcal{J}_{d-1} + \mathcal{J}_{d+1} )\bigg]$
    \item $\displaystyle \Phi^0_{d,4|\Gamma } = \eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{4-d} \bigg[ \frac{3\mu_{\rm r}^{4} t_{1}t_{2}t_{3} + \mu_{\rm r}^2 (t_{1}+t_{3})}{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-4} - \mathcal{J}_{d+4} )$\\[-1ex]
    \hbox to \linewidth{\hfill $\displaystyle {}+ \frac{3\mu_{\rm r}^{4} t_{1}t_{2}(t_{1}+t_{3}) + \mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1}(2k_{\rm r}-3)+\mu_{\rm r}^2 t_{3} }{3} \,(\mathcal{J}_{d-2} - \mathcal{J}_{d+2} ) \bigg]$.}
\end{itemize}

\underline{Case $b=2$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} In this case, $a$ is odd (because $\gcd(a,b)=1$) so we have $t_{1}=\operatorname{cotan}(a \frac{\pi }{2} )=0$ and $t_{3}=\operatorname{cotan}(3a \frac{\pi }{2} )=0$. Thus $\Phi^0_{d,2|\Gamma } =0$, which implies $\Phi^0_{d,2} =0$ by \cref{eq: pb verifie par mcl qd n>0,pb de Helmholtz dans A Omega}. If we compare this to the formula ``$\Phi^0_{d,2} = \Gamma (d+1) \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{2-d} \frac{\mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1}}{\sin (2\Theta )} \,(\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d-2} + \mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d+2} )$'' given by \cref{ex: expression sing heterog CL} when $2\leqslant b-1$, we notice that the problem of the division by $\sin (2\Theta )=0$ is solved here by the fact that $t_{1}=0$.\\
Next, one can verify that we have \begin{align*}
    \Phi^0_{d,3|\Gamma } &= \cancel{\mu_{\rm r} \partial _{y} \Phi^0_{d,2|\Gamma } } + \frac{\mu_{\rm r}}{3} (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )\partial _{y} \Phi^0_{d,0|\Gamma } \\
    & =\eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{3-d} \Big[ \frac{\mu_{\rm r}}{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-3} + \mathcal{J}_{d+3} ) + \frac{\mu_{\rm r}}{3} (k_{\rm r}-1) \. (\mathcal{J}_{d-1} + \mathcal{J}_{d+1} )\Big].
\end{align*}
This is similar to the formula of $\Phi^0_{d,3|\Gamma }$ when $3\leqslant b$, but with a few terms less because here $\Phi^0_{d,2} =0$. Continuing the calculations, one similarly obtains the reduced formula:
\[\Phi^0_{d,4|\Gamma } = \eta \,\Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{4-d} \bigg[ \frac{\mu_{\rm r}^2 (t_{1}+t_{3})}{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-4} - \mathcal{J}_{d+4} ) + \frac{\mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1}(2k_{\rm r}-3)+\mu_{\rm r}^2 t_{3} }{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-2} - \mathcal{J}_{d+2} ) \bigg].\]
Since $t_{1}=t_{3}=0$, this yields $\Phi^0_{d,4|\Gamma } =0$ and $\Phi^0_{d,4} =0$.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Case $b=4$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Given \cref{expression sing heterog CL}, we already know that, when $n\leqslant 3$, $\Phi^0_{d,n}$ is a linear combination of the $\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d+m}$ with $|m|\leqslant n$. As~for $\Phi^0_{d,4}$, since $\gcd(a,b)=1$, we have $2a\equiv 2\,[{4}]$ and $\{a,3a\}\equiv \{a,-a\}\equiv \{1,-1\}$ modulo 4. Hence $t_{2}=0$ and $t_{1} +t_{3} =\operatorname{cotan}( \frac{\pi }{4} )+\operatorname{cotan}(- \frac{\pi }{4} )=0$. Thus the expression of $\Phi^0_{d,4|\Gamma }$ given at the beginning of this proof reduces to
\[\Phi^0_{d,4|\Gamma } = \eta \, \Gamma (d+1)\, \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{4-d} \frac{\mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1}(2k_{\rm r}-3)+\mu_{\rm r}^2 t_{3} }{3} (\mathcal{J}_{d-2} - \mathcal{J}_{d+2} ).\]
So $\Phi^0_{d,4} = \Gamma (d+1)\. \left( \frac{k_{0} }{2} \right)^{4-d} \frac{\mu_{\rm r}^2  t_{1}(2k_{\rm r}-3)+\mu_{\rm r}^2 t_{3}}{3\sin (2\Theta )} (\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d-2} + \mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d+2} )$, which is well-defined because we do~not have to divide by $\sin (4\Theta )=0$ thanks to the absence of terms involving $\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d\pm 4}$.
<!-- end demo-91 -->
<!-- demo-92: body_md -->
The proof is similar to \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}. We only give the main ideas, as the details are quite cumbersome, especially for $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}$, like in \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}.\medskip

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us first treat $c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$. By~\cref{expression de Rmacro phi avec les mcl}, we have when $p-d<\beta $:
\[c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } := \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \langle \@ifnextchar^{(\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon)}{\mathcal{R}^+_\epsilon}\rangle  (\phi_{d'} ) = \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0}^\infty \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \bigg) = \sigma _{d,p,\ell } \circ  \mathcal{H}_\epsilon \circ  \bigg( \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0} ^{\textcolor{red!93!black}{\beta -1}} \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \bigg).\]
By~definition of $\beta $, there exist complex numbers $a_{d',n,m}$ and $b_{d',n,m}$ s.t.\ we have for~any $n\in [\![0,\beta -1]\!]$:
\[\Phi^0_{d',n} = \sum _{m=-n} ^{n} \big(a_{d',n,m} \,\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{d'+m} + b_{d',n,m} \,\mathcal{J}^\Omega_{d'+m} \big).\]
By~definition of $\mathcal{Y}^\Omega_{j}$ for $j\in \mathbb{Z}$ in \cref{eq: def BesselYOmega_n}, this implies that, for~any $q<-d'-n$, the component of $\Phi^0_{d',n}$ in $\mathcal{A}_{q} (\Omega )$ does~not involve $\log (\alpha z)$. Hence, under the assumptions $p-d<\beta $ and $p+d'<0$, the component of $\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0} ^{\beta -1} \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n}$ in $\epsilon ^{p-d} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$ does~not involve $\log (\alpha z)$ (because $d<-d'-(p-d)$), which yields that the component of $\mathcal{H}_\epsilon\big(\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{n=0} ^{\beta -1} \epsilon ^{n} \.\Phi^0_{d',n} \big)$ in $\epsilon ^{p} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )[\ln \epsilon ]$ does~not involve $\ln \epsilon $. The rest of this step is similar to \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel,valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} This is essentially a technical adaptation of the second step of the proof of \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel} (that is already technical). The main idea of that previous proof is explained in \cref{fig: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}. Here we only illustrate in \cref{fig: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise} how this idea is modified. The main difference between \cref{fig: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise,fig: preuve valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel} is that the green zone is an infinite band in the first one whereas it~is a parallelogram in the latter one. This is linked to the new equalities of \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise 2} (written in red) that do~not appear in  \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel}.
<!-- end demo-92 -->
<!-- demo-93: body_md -->
We recall that we have
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalisation preuve 1}}
    c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } := \! \sum _{\substack{(p_{1} ,p_{2} )\in (\mathbb{N}-d)\times (\mathbb{N}+d')\\ n\in \mathbb{N},\, p_{1} +p_{2} +2n=p}}
    \ \sum _{\substack{d_{1} \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p_{1} +d_{1} \in \mathbb{N}}} \ \sum _{\substack{d_{2} \in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p_{2} -d_{2} \in \mathbb{N}}}
    \ \sum _{\substack{(\ell _{1} ,\ell _{2} )\in \mathbb{N}^2 \\ \ell _{1} +\ell _{2} =\ell }}
    c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d_{1} ,p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }\cdot \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,n} )\cdot c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,d'\!,p_{2} ,\ell _{2} } .
\end{equation}
Let us show that any non-zero term satisfies
\[p_{1} +d_{1} <\beta  \text{ and } p_{2} -d_{2} <\beta  \text{ and } (d_{1} \not\in -\mathbb{N} \text{ or } p_{1} +d<-2d_{1} ) \text{ and } (d'\not\in -\mathbb{N} \text{ or } p_{2} +d'<0)\]
in order to apply \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise 1,valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise 2}. We do it by contraposition, by showing that if a non-zero term verifies
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalisation preuve 2}}
    p_{1} +d_{1} \geqslant \beta  \text{ or } p_{2} -d_{2} \geqslant \beta  \text{ or } (d_{1} \in -\mathbb{N} \text{ and } p_{1} +d\geqslant -2d_{1} ) \text{ or } (d'\in -\mathbb{N} \text{ and } p_{2} +d'\geqslant 0)
\end{equation}
then we do~not have $\big[p<\min (\beta ,2b+2\tau) \text{ and } (d'\in -\mathbb{N} \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  p<b+\tau)\big]$, which means that we have                                                                                                            
\[\textstyle p\geqslant \beta  \text{ or } p\geqslant 2b+2\tau \text{ or } (d'\in -\mathbb{N} \text{ and } p\geqslant b+\tau).\]
Let us treat separately each subcase of \cref{eq: valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalisation preuve 2}.
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let us assume $p_{1} +d_{1} \geqslant \beta $. If $d_{1} >0$, then $\sigma _{d_{1}} (\mathcal{S} ^{\infty } _{d_{2} ,n} ) =\delta _{d_{1} ,d_{2}} \delta _{n,0}$. Since we are looking at a non-zero term, we have $d_{1} =d_{2}$ and $n=0$. Thus $p=(p_{1} +d_{1} ) +(p_{2} -d_{2} ) \geqslant \beta +0$. Otherwise, we have $d_{1} <0$, which yields $p=(p_{1} +d_{1} )-d_{1} +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n \geqslant \beta +0+0+0+0=\beta $.
    \item If $p_{2} -d_{2} \geqslant \beta $, then $p=(p_{1} +d)-d +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n\geqslant 0+0+\beta +0+0=\beta $.
    \item If $d_{1} \in -\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{1} +d\geqslant -2d_{1}$, then $d_{1} \leqslant -b$ (because $\mathbb{Z}\cap \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}=b\mathbb{Z}$), so $p=(p_{1} +d)-d +(p_{2} -d_{2} )+d_{2} +2n\geqslant 2b+\tau+0+\tau+0=2b+2\tau$.
    \item If $d' \in -\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{2} +d'\geqslant 0$, then $d' \leqslant -b$, so $p=(p_{1} +d)-d +(p_{2} +d')-d' +2n\geqslant 0+\tau+0+b+0=b+\tau$.
\end{itemize}
By~\cref{valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise 1,valeur de cmaicro cas rationnel generalise 2} we deduce that any non-zero term of \cref{eq: valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalisation preuve 1} satisfies $d=d_{1}$, $d_{2} =d'$, $p_{1} =-d$, $p_{2} =d$, $\ell _{1} =\ell _{2} =0$ and $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow S}_{d,d_{1} ,p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }=c^{S\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d_{2} ,d'\!,p_{2} ,\ell _{2} }=1$. This implies the desired formula.
<!-- end demo-93 -->
<!-- demo-94: body_md -->
The proof is similar to \cref{simplifications cas rationnel}. Let $p<p_{\min }$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$. \Cref{construction directe des upl} states:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 1}}
    \sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) = \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ 2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) .
\end{equation}
Let us show that the right-hand side of \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 1} is equal to
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 2}}
    \sum _{\substack{n\in \mathbb{N}\\ 2n\leqslant p+d}} \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\leqslant p+d-2n}} \omega ^{2n} \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d',n} )\cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p-d'+d-2n,0} )
\end{equation}
(which, when $\ell =0$, is the right-hand side of \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel}). If $p< \frac{2b}{a} =2\tau$, then the sums in \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 1,eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 2} are both empty, so they vanish. Now, let us assume $p<\min (\beta ,2b \frac{a+1}{a} )$. Any non-zero term in the right-hand side of \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 1} satisfies $p-p'\leqslant p<\min (\beta ,2b+2\tau)$ because $2b \frac{a+1}{a} = 2b+2\tau$. In addition, if $d'\in -\mathbb{N}$, we also have $-b\geqslant d'\geqslant p'-\tau$ by \cref{precision de l'ansatz sur uDA}, so $p'\geqslant b+\tau$, which yields $p-p'\leqslant 2b+2\tau-(b+\tau)=b+\tau$. Therefore we can apply \cref{valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalise} to any non-zero term of \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 1}, which shows that it~is equal to \cref{eq: simplifications cas rationnel version forte preuve 2}. The rest is identical to the proof of \cref{simplifications cas rationnel}, except the last statement about $b\not\in \{1,3\}$.\\
Finally, let us prove the last statement.
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $b\geqslant 5$, then we have $p_{\min } \geqslant  \min \!\left( \beta  ,\, 2b\. \frac{a+1}{a} \right) \geqslant  \min (b,2b)\geqslant 5$ because $\beta \geqslant b$ by \cref{expression sing heterog CL}.
    \item If $b\in \{2,4\}$, then $p_{\min } \geqslant  \min \!\left( \beta  ,\, 2b\. \frac{a+1}{a} \right) =\min (\beta ,2b+2\tau)\geqslant  \min (5,2\cdot 2+2\cdot  \frac{1}{2} )=5$ by \cref{expression sing heterog CL b=2 ou 4}.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end demo-94 -->
<!-- paragraphesansboite-11: body_md -->
Let $R_{\mathrm{s}} := \operatorname{dist}(0,\operatorname{supp}f_{\mathrm{s}})$. Since we assumed $\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma ,\operatorname{supp}f_{\mathrm{s}})>0$, we have $R_{\mathrm{s}}>0$. In addition, all over this section, $C_{\dots }$ will denote any positive constant that depends \emph{only} on the variables in ``...'' and on $(\Theta ,\mu _{0} ,\mu _{1} ,\rho _{0} ,\rho _{1} ,\omega )$. Its value may change from line to line.
<!-- end paragraphesansboite-11 -->
<!-- demo-95: body_md -->
Let $f $ be in $\@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$, resp.\ $\@AGprecisd,n\@AGprecis$. It~is easy to see that the decomposition of $f $ on the basis of $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$, resp.\ $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Gamma )$, mentioned in \cref{def: norme sur A_d} only involves elements of the basis that are also in $\@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$, resp.\ $\@AGprecisd,n\@AGprecis$. Therefore, it suffices to verify that $R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}$, $R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}$, $\partial _{y|\Gamma }$ and $\partial _{x|\Gamma }$ send the elements of these basis into the right spaces.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $j\in [\![0,2n]\!]$ and $f :x\mapsto x^{d} \ln ^{j} x$. The proof of \cref{operateurs R dans Omega} shows that $R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )=\Im[(\alpha z)^{d} P(\log (\alpha z))]$ with $P:=L_{d}(T^{j} )$. By~\cref{resolution de Im[alphad P(T-iTheta)]=Q}, we have $\deg P=j+1$ if $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}$ and $\deg P=j$ otherwise. Therefore, it~is easy to check that $R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$.
    \item Let $f :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log ^{j} \!(\alpha z)]$ be an element of the basis of $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$ s.t.\ $f \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$. The proof of \cref{operateurs R dans Omega} shows that $R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )=\psi -R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(\psi _{|\Gamma } )$ with $\psi :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q+1} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k+1} P(\log (\alpha z))]$ and $4(k+1)\big((q+1)P+P'\big)=T^{j}$. Using point 1, it suffices to show that $\psi \in \@AOprecisd+2,n,\delta \@AOprecis$. But this is easy by writing $q-k\geqslant \delta  \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  (q+1)-(k+1)\geqslant \delta $ and:
    \begin{alignat*}{2}
        \deg P &\leqslant  j + \delta _{q,-1} && \text{ because }  \deg ((q+1)P+P')=j \\
        &\leqslant  2n-1+ \mathbf{1}_{\@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}} (q-k) +\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{N}} (q) + \delta _{q,-1} && \text{ because }  f \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis\\
        &\leqslant  2n-1+ \mathbf{1}_{\@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}} \big((q+1)-(k+1)\big) +\mathbf{1}_{\mathbb{N}} (q+1)
    \end{alignat*}
    \item Let $f :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log ^{j} \!(\alpha z)]$ be an element of the basis of $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$ s.t.\ $f \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$. The proof of \cref{operateurs de derivation dans A} shows that $\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } = x^{q+k-1} \Re[\alpha ^{q-k} P(\ln x-\mathrm{i}\Theta )]$ with $P:=((q-k)T^{j} +jT^{j-1} )$. Since $\deg P\leqslant j\leqslant 2n+1$, we have $\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } \in \@AGprecisd-1,n+1\@AGprecis$.
    \item Let $j\in [\![0,2n-1]\!]$ and $f :x\mapsto x^{d} \ln ^{j} x$. We have $\partial _{x} f  = x^{d-1} (d\ln ^{j} x+ j\ln ^{j-1} x) \in \@AGprecisd,n\@AGprecis$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end demo-95 -->
<!-- demo-96: body_md -->
Similarly to the proof of \cref{action des op R sur A precis}, it suffices to show these inequalities when $f $ is an element of the basis mentioned in \cref{def: norme sur A_d}. For~any $P=\sum_{j=0}^m a_{j} T^{j} \in \mathbb{C}[T]$, we denote $\|P\|:=\sum_{j=0}^m |a_{j} |$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $j\in [\![0,2n-1]\!]$ and $f :x\mapsto x^{d} \ln ^{j} x$. We have $R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )=\Im[(\alpha z)^{d} P(\log (\alpha z))]$ with $P(T):=L_{d}(T^{j} )$. In addition, $L_{d}$ (which maps any $Q\in \mathbb{R}[T]$ to a solution of $\Im[\alpha ^{d} P(T-\mathrm{i}\Theta )]=Q$, see \cref{resolution de Im[alphad P(T-iTheta)]=Q}) only depends on $\alpha ^{d} = e^{-\mathrm{i}\Theta d}$, so it only depends on $d \,\mathrm{mod}\, \tau=d \,\mathrm{mod}\, \frac{b}{a}$, which can take only a finite number of values since $d\in \frac1a\mathbb{Z}$. Thus
    \[\sup _{d\in \frac1a\mathbb{Z}} \sup _{j\in [\![0,2n-1]\!]} \|L_{d}(T^{j} )\| = C_{n} < +\infty \]
    Therefore $\|R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\| = \|P\|\leqslant C_{n} = C_{n} \|f \|$.
    \item Let $f :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log ^{j} \!(\alpha z)]$ be an element of the basis of $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$ s.t.\ $f \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$. The proof of \cref{operateurs R dans Omega} shows that $R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )=\psi -R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(\psi _{|\Gamma } )$ with $\psi :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q+1} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k+1} P(\log (\alpha z))]$ and $4(k+1)\big((q+1)P+P'\big)=T^{j}$. Using point 1, it suffices to show that
    \[\|\psi \|\leqslant  \left\{\begin{array}{@{\;}ll}
        \frac{C_{n} }{d+1}  & \text{if } d>|\delta |\\[1ex]
        C_{\delta ,n}  & \text{if } d<|\delta |
    \end{array}\right.\]
    First let us asume that $d\geqslant |\delta |$. \Cref{rq: lien entre d q k delta} implies $2q\geqslant d+\delta \geqslant 0$. Let $D$ be the derivation operator of $\mathbb{R}_{2n+1} [T] :=\{Q\in \mathbb{R}[T] \mid \deg Q\leqslant 2n+1\}$ and $C^{D} _{n}$ its continuity constant for $\|.\|$. Using $j\leqslant 2n+1$, $D^{2n+3} =0$ and $q\geqslant 0$, we get:
    \[P = \frac{1}{4(k+1)(q+1)} \left( \mathrm{id}+ \frac{1}{q+1} D\right)^{-1} (T^{j} ) = \frac{1}{4(k+1)} \sum _{m=0} ^{2n+1} \frac{(-1)^{m} }{(q+1)^{m+1} } D^{m} (T^{j} )\]
    so 
    \[\|P\| \leqslant  \frac{1}{4(k+1)} \sum _{m=0} ^{2n+1} \frac{\|D^{m} (T^{j} )\|}{(q+1)^{m+1} } \leqslant  \frac{1}{4(k+1)} \sum _{m=0} ^{2n+1} \frac{(2n+1) !}{q+1} \leqslant  \frac{C_{n} }{(q+1)(k+1)}.\]
    Moreover, $(q+1)(k+1)=qk+q+k+1\geqslant d+1$, as $d=q+k$ and $q,k\geqslant 0$. Therefore $\|\psi \| = \|P\|\leqslant  C_{n} /(d+1)$.\\
    Now, let us assume $d<|\delta |$. By~\cref{rq: lien entre d q k delta}, we also have $d\geqslant \delta $, so $\delta <0$ and $d\in [\delta ,-\delta ]\cap \frac1a\mathbb{Z}$. In addition, $k\leqslant  \frac{d-\delta }{2} \leqslant |\delta |$ and $j\leqslant 2n+1$. Thus $q=d-k$ and $k$ and $j$ can take only a finite number of values that depends on $(\delta ,n)$. Hence $\|\psi \|\leqslant C_{\delta ,n}$.
    \item Let $f :=\Im[(\alpha z)^{q} \,\overline{\alpha z}^{k} \log ^{j} \!(\alpha z)]$ be an element of the basis of $\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )$ s.t.\ $f \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$. We know that $\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } = x^{q+k-1} \Re[\alpha ^{q-k} P(\ln x-\mathrm{i}\Theta )]$ with $P(T):=((q-k)T^{j} +jT^{j-1} )$. Hence $\|\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } \|\leqslant \|P(\ln x-\mathrm{i}\Theta )\| \leqslant  C_{n} \|P\|\leqslant C_{n} \,(|q-k|+1)$ because $j\leqslant 2n+1$. Finally, we have $q-k\geqslant \delta $ by \cref{def: norme sur A_d} and $q-k\leqslant q+k=d$, so $|q-k|\leqslant \max (-\delta ,d)\leqslant \max (|\delta |,d)$.
    \item Let $j\in [\![0,2n-1]\!]$ and $f :x\mapsto x^{d} \ln ^{j} x$. We have $\|\partial _{x} f \| = \|x^{d-1} (d\ln ^{j} x+ j\ln ^{j-1} x)\|\leqslant C_{n} (1+|d|)\leqslant C_{n} (1+\max (|\delta |,d))$ as $d\geqslant \delta $.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end demo-96 -->
<!-- demo-97: body_md -->
The proof uses the results of \cref{action des op R sur A precis,norme naive des op R}.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item It suffices to multiply $\|R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\| \leqslant  C_{n} \,\|f \|$ by $\gamma (d)$ as $R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$.
    \item If $d\geqslant \max (|\delta |,1)$, then $\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|_\gamma=\sqrt{\Gamma (d+2)}\,\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|\leqslant  \sqrt{\Gamma (d+2)} \frac{C_{n} }{d+1} \|f \| = \sqrt{\frac{\Gamma (d)d}{d+1}} C_{n} \|f \|$ $\leqslant $ $\sqrt{\Gamma (d)} \,C_{n} \|f \|=C_{n} \|f \|_\gamma$.\\
    If $|\delta |\leqslant d<\max (|\delta |,1)$, then $0\leqslant d<1$, so $\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|_\gamma\leqslant  C \|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|\leqslant  C_{n} \|f \| \leqslant  C_{n} \|f \|_\gamma$.\\
    Otherwise, $d<|\delta |$ so $\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|_\gamma\leqslant  C_{\delta } \|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f )\|\leqslant  C_{n,\delta } \|f \| \leqslant  C_{n,\delta } \|f \|_\gamma$.
    \item We have $\|\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } \|_\gamma \leqslant  C_{n} \,f_{\delta } (d) \|f \|_\gamma$ with $f_{\delta } (d):=(1+\max (d,-\delta )) \frac{\gamma (d-1)}{\gamma (d)}$. $f_{\delta }$ satisfies $f_{\delta } (d)=O(\sqrt{d} )=O(s^{d} )$ when $d\rightarrow \infty $. Moreover, \cref{rq: lien entre d q k delta} states that $\@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis \neq \{0\}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}} d\geqslant \delta $, so we can assume that $d\geqslant \delta $. Hence we have $\|\partial _{y} f _{|\Gamma } \|_\gamma \leqslant  C_{\delta ,n,s} s^{d} \|f \|_\gamma$.
    \item Similar to 3.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end demo-97 -->
<!-- demo-98: body_md -->
All the inclusions are straightforward consequences of \cref{action des op R sur A precis}, except $\langle -k_{0} ^2 R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}\rangle (\@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )) \subset  \@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$. Let us prove it. Let $\Phi  \in \@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$. By~$R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(\@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )) \subset  \@AMprecisn,\delta +2\@AMprecis(\Omega )$ and \cref{rq: inclusions entre les AMprecis}, $\@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$ is stable under $R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}$. Thus, $(-k_{0} ^2 R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}})^{m} \Phi  \in  \@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$ for~any $m\in \mathbb{N}$. Now, $\@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$ is closed under $\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}$ according to \cref{fsum de sev des Ed}, so $\langle -k_{0} ^2 R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}\rangle (\Phi ) = \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{m=0} ^{\infty } (-k_{0} ^2 R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}})^{m} (\Phi ) \in \@AMprecisn,\delta \@AMprecis(\Omega )$.

<!-- demo-99: body_md -->
The proof uses the results of \cref{action des op R sur A precis,norme-gamma des op R}.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Writing $\Phi $ as $\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d} f _{d}$, it suffices to multiply $\|R_{\mathrm{D}}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f _{d} )\|_\gamma \leqslant  C_{n} \|f _{d} \|_\gamma$ by $s^{-d}$ and to sum over $d$.
    \item Let $(f _{d} )$ be s.t.\ $f _{d} \in \@AOprecisd,n,\delta \@AOprecis$ for~any $d$ and $\Phi =\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d} f _{d}$. Then
    \[\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(\Phi )\|_{s} =\Big\| \operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d} \underbrace{R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f _{d-2} )}_{\in \,\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )} \Big\|_{s} = \sum _{d} s^{-d} \,\|R_{\Delta}^{\raisebox{1pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle \Omega$}}(f _{d-2} )\|_\gamma \leqslant  C_{\delta ,n} \sum _{d} s^{-d} \|f _{d-2} \|_\gamma = C_{\delta ,n} \,s^{-2} \,\|\Phi \|_{s} .\]
    \item Let $(f _{d} )$ be s.t.\ $f _{d} \in \@AGprecisd,n\@AGprecis$ for~any $d$ and $\Phi =\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d} f _{d}$. Then
    \begin{multline*}
        \|\partial _{y} \Phi _{|\Gamma } \|_{s'} = \Big\|\operatorname*{\mathchoice
        {\contour*{.}{$\displaystyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\textstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptstyle\sum$}} 
        {\contour*{.}{$\scriptscriptstyle\sum$}}}_{d} \underbrace{\partial _{y} f _{d+1|\Gamma } }_{\in \,\mathcal{A}_{d} (\Gamma )} \|_{s'} = \sum _{d} s'^{-d} \,\|\partial _{y} f _{d+1|\Gamma } \|_\gamma = s' \sum _{d} s'^{-d} \,\|\partial _{y} f _{d|\Gamma } \|_\gamma \\[-3ex]
        \leqslant  s'\, C_{\delta ,n, s'/s } \sum _{d} s'^{-d} \, \Big( \frac{s'}{s} \Big)^{d} \|f _{d} \|_\gamma = C_{\delta ,n,s,s'} \,\|\Phi \|_{s} .
    \end{multline*}\vspace{-3.5ex}
    \item Very similar to 3.
\end{enumerate}
