<!-- demo-114: body_md -->
\defD^N_{#,\ell,n}1{D^N_{#1,\ell,n}}                                 
\def\ell_{m}{\ell_{m}} 
\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} First, let us express $\sum _{d} \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \,\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} $ in terms of the modal decompositions of the far fields. By~\cref{eq: def mse,eq: sigma de sclDA}, we have
\begin{align*}
	\sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} 
	&= \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \left(\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } ) \right) \left( \sum _{n=0} ^{m-1} \epsilon ^{n} \Phi^{N}_{d,n} \right) \\
	&= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{n=0} ^{m-1} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p+n} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )\cdot  \Phi^{N}_{d,n} \\
	&= \sum _{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,2m)} \sum _{\substack{n\in [\![0,m-1]\!]\\ p'-n\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)}} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p'} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \! \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p'-n,\ell } )\cdot  \Phi^{N}_{d,n}
	\refstepcounter{equation}\tag{\theequation}\label{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 1}
\end{align*}
using the change of index $p':=p+n$. Since we have $u_{p,\ell } =0$ for any $p\in \mathbb{R} \setminus \mathbb{P}$ by convention, the condition $p'-n \in \mathbb{P}$ in \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 1} can be deleted. Similarly, \Cref{precision de l'ansatz sur uDA} implies that $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )=0$ when $d<-p+\tau$. So the condition $-m\leqslant d$ in \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 1} can be replaced by $-p'+n+\tau\leqslant d$ (as $p'-n=p\leqslant m$). In addition, the condition $p'-n\in [0,m)$ is equivalent to $p'-m<n\leqslant p'$. To simplify the calculations, let us denote
\[D^N_{p,\ell,n} := \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ \textcolor{red!93!black}{-p+n+\tau}\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p-n,\ell } )\cdot  \Phi^{N}_{d,n} .\]
Thus, we obtain:
\begin{align}
	\smash{\sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -p+m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}}} \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} 
	&= \sum _{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,2m)} \, \sum _{n\in [\![0,m-1]\!]\cap (p'-m,p']}\, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p'} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  D^N_{p',\ell,n} \nonumber \\
	&= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \sum _{n=0} ^{\lfloor {p}\rfloor } D^N_{p,\ell,n}
	+ \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [m,2m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \sum _{n=\lfloor {p-m}\rfloor +1} ^{m} D^N_{p,\ell,n} . \label{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 2}
\end{align}
We notice that the first term of \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 2} is the sum of the total modal decompositions of the far fields of order $p\leqslant m$, while the second term is a kind of boundary term that contains only parts of the modal decompositions of the next far fields.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} For~any $f\in H^{1} _{\mathrm{loc}} (\Omega )$ and $(r,\theta )$, let us denote $|f|_{r,\theta } := |f(r,\theta )|+r|\nabla  f(r,\theta )|$. We claim that we have for~any $p\in \mathbb{P}$ and $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve decompo modale des CL generalisee}}
	\bigg|u_{p,\ell } - \sum _{n=0} ^{\lfloor {p}\rfloor } D^N_{p,\ell,n} \bigg|_{r,\theta } \leqslant C_{p,f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left( \frac{r}{R} \right)^{(N+1)\tau -\lfloor {p}\rfloor } \langle \ln r\rangle^{2p+1} .
\end{equation}
Indeed, \cref{decompo modale des CL} proves this result in the case where $\Phi^{N}_{d,n} =\Phi^{\rm lim}_{d,n}$ for~any $(d,n)$, while \cref{decompo en modes tronques des CL} treats the case where $\Phi^{N}_{d,n} =T_{<(N+1)\tau} (\Phi^0_{d,n} )$ for~any $(d,n)$. Here we are in a mixed situation where, for~any $n$, we have either $\Phi^{N}_{d,n} =\Phi^{\rm lim}_{d,n}$ for~any $d$, or $\Phi^{N}_{d,n} =T_{<(N+1)\tau} (\Phi^0_{d,n} )$ for~any $d$. Since the proofs of \cref{decompo modale des CL,decompo en modes tronques des CL} treat separately the different values of $n$, it~is easy to generalize these theorems to our situation, which proves \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve decompo modale des CL generalisee}. Multiplying \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve decompo modale des CL generalisee} by $\epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon $ and summing over $(p,\ell )$, we get:
\[\bigg|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}} - \!\! \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \sum _{n=0} ^{\lfloor {p}\rfloor } D^N_{p,\ell,n} \bigg|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  \left( \frac{r}{R} \right)^{(N+1)\tau -p} \langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1} .\]
Let $\delta :=\tau- \frac{1}{2} >0$. For~any $p>0$, we have $\epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  r^{\tau-p} = \epsilon ^{\delta } \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  \big( \frac{\epsilon }{r} \big)^{p-\delta } \cdot  r^{1/2} \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},\ell } \,M^{p-\delta } \,r^{1/2}$ because $\epsilon  \leqslant Mr\leqslant MR_{\mathrm{s}}$. This yields
\[\bigg|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}} - \!\! \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \sum _{n=0} ^{\lfloor {p}\rfloor } D^N_{p,\ell,n} \bigg|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R,M} \left( \frac{r}{R} \right)^{N\tau + \frac{1}{2} } \langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1.}\]
                                                                                       
Given \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve 2}, it only remains to prove
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve estimation terme 2}}
	\bigg|\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [m,2m)} \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell_{m}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \sum _{n=\lfloor {p-m}\rfloor +1} ^{m} D^N_{p,\ell,n} \bigg|_{r,\theta } \leqslant C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R,M} \,\. \epsilon ^{m} \.r^{\tau-m} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1} .
\end{equation}
To begin, let us estimate each $D^N_{p,\ell,n}$. This part is similar to the proof of \cref{convergence des series de mcl}. By~\cref{estimation des mcl}, we know that, for~any $s>1$, $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap [-m,\infty )$, $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $0<r\leqslant R$ and $\forall \theta \in [0,\Theta ]$, we have
\[|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} (r,\theta )|_{r,\theta } \;\leqslant \; C_{n,R,s} \,(s r)^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} .\]
Let $R':=(2R+R_{\mathrm{s}})/3$ and $R'' :=(R+2R_{\mathrm{s}})/3$. We have $R<R'<R''<R_{\mathrm{s}}$. \Cref{decompo modale des CL} states that $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) \leqslant  C_{p,f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \,R''^{-d}$. Hence we have
\[|D^N_{p,\ell,n}|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{p,n,f_{\mathrm{s}},s,R} \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -p+n+\tau\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} R''^{-d} \cdot  (s r)^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} \vspace{-1ex}\]
Taking $s := \frac{R''}{R'}$, we obtain:
\begin{align*}
	\epsilon ^{p} \,|D^N_{p,\ell,n}|_{r,\theta } &\leqslant  \epsilon ^{p} \cdot C_{p,n,f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -p+n+\tau\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \left( \frac{r}{R'} \right)^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} \\
	&= \epsilon ^{p} \cdot  C_{p,n,f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \, \frac{1}{1-\left( \frac{r}{R'} \right)^{\pi/\Theta} } \left( \frac{r}{R'} \right)^{-p+\tau} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{p,n,f_{\mathrm{s}},R,M} \,\. \epsilon ^{m} \.r^{\tau-m} \.\langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1} 
\end{align*}
because $(\epsilon /r)^{p-m} \leqslant  M^{p-m}$. Summing over $(p,\ell ,n)$, this yields \cref{eq: decompo modale SE 1 preuve estimation terme 2} and concludes the proof.
<!-- end demo-114 -->
<!-- demo-115: body_md -->
Let us prove by induction on $p$. The property is trivial for $p=0$, so let us assume $p>0$. Let us assume that we have $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$. Then we have
\begin{itemize}
	\item either $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$, which directly implies $p\in \mathbb{P}+2\tau$ and $p+d-d'\in \mathbb{N}$ by \cref{coefs cfinal non nuls},
	\item or the complicated sum in \cref{eq: def cme} is non empty. In this case, let $(p_{1} ,p_{2} ,\ell _{1} ,\ell _{2} ,d'')$ be the index of one of the terms of this sum. Then we have $p=p_{1} +p_{2} \in (\mathbb{P}+2\tau)+(\mathbb{P}+2\tau)\subset \mathbb{P}+2\tau$ and $p+d-d' = (p_{1} +d-d'')+(p_{2} +d''-d') \in \mathbb{N}+\mathbb{N}=\mathbb{N}$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end demo-115 -->
<!-- demo-116: body_md -->
Let us prove the property by induction on $p$. When $p=0$, the right-hand sides of \cref{eq: condition de coin CL iteree} and \cref{eq: rappel ME de condition de coin CL} both vanish thanks to the conditions on the index $p'$. This proves \cref{eq: condition de coin CL iteree} in this case.\\
Now, let us assume $p>0$. Let $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ and $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$. For~any $(d',p',\ell ')$, let us denote $\tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p',\ell '} := c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p',\ell '} - c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p',\ell '}$. In addition, for any family $(x_{p',\ell '} )$, let us denote $x_{\bullet} :=(x_{p',\ell '} )$ the family itself. We also denote $*$ the convolution product w.r.t.\ $(p',\ell ')$.\\
\Cref{coefs cfinal non nuls,coefs cme non nuls} show that the conditions ``$(p_{1} ,p_{2} )\in (\mathbb{P}+2\tau)^2 $'' and ``$d''\in (d+p_{1} -\mathbb{N})\cap (d'-p_{2} +\mathbb{N})$'' in \cref{eq: def cme} are not necessary because removing them only adds null terms. Therefore, we have
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: condition de coin CL iteree preuve cmebis}}
	\tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} = \sum _{d''\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',\bullet} *c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',\bullet} .
\end{equation}
                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
Similarly, using \cref{ansatz sur Aeps,coefs cfinal non nuls,coefs cme non nuls}, one can verify that \cref{eq: condition de coin CL iteree} rewrites as
\[\sigma _{d} (u^0_{\bullet} ) = \!\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} )\]
while \cref{eq: rappel ME de condition de coin CL} is equivalent to
\[\sigma _{d} (u^0_{\bullet} ) = \!\sum _{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) .\]
Now, by~definition of $\tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}$, we have
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: condition de coin CL iteree preuve sep en 2 bouts}}
	\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) = \sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) + \sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} \tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ).
\end{equation}
Let us focus on the second term. \Cref{eq: condition de coin CL iteree preuve cmebis} implies
\begin{align*}
	\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} \tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} )
	&= \sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} \bigg(\sum _{d''\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',\bullet} *c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',\bullet} \bigg) *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} )\\
	&= \sum _{d''\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',\bullet} *\bigg( \sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*}  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) \bigg)
\end{align*}
because $*$ is associative and the above infinite sums are actually finite for each value of $(p,\ell )$. In~particular, at rank $(p,\ell )$ we have
\[\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} \tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) \Big|_{p,\ell } = \sum _{p',\ell '} \sum _{d''\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \bigg( \sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*}  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) \bigg)\bigg|_{p',\ell '}\]
where ``$|_{p',\ell '}$'' means that the result of the convolution is evaluated at a given $(p',\ell ')$. By~\cref{coefs cfinal non nuls}, we have $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \neq 0 \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+2\tau$, so the non zero terms of the above sum satisfy $p'<p$. Hence we can apply the induction hypothesis on them, which yields
\[\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} \tilde{c}^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} ) \Big|_{p,\ell } = \sum _{p',\ell '} \sum _{d''\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d''} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ).\]
Adding the first term of \cref{eq: condition de coin CL iteree preuve sep en 2 bouts}, we finally obtain
\[\sum _{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\bullet} *\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\bullet} )\Big|_{p,\ell } =\sum _{p',\ell '} \sum _{d''\in \textcolor{red!93!black}{\@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*}} c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d''} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) =\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } ) .\]
<!-- end demo-116 -->
<!-- demo-117: body_md -->
Let us show the property $\mathcal{P}$ defined as ``for any $(d,d',p,\ell )\in (-\tau\mathbb{N}^*)\times (\tau\mathbb{N}^*)\times \mathbb{P}\times \mathbb{N}$, if $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$ then $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero''. Note that the statement ``$c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$'' depends on the values of $\mu _{0} ,\mu _{1} ,\rho _{0} ,\rho _{1} ,\omega $ and the corner profile coefficients, while ``$\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero'' is independant of it. The property $\mathcal{P}$ implies the desired result because, by construction of $\ell _{p}$, if $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero then $\ell \leqslant \ell _{p}$.\\
The general idea is the following. The expression of $\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )$ given by \cref{condition de coin CL iteree} contains a term $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{0,0} )$ where $\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{0,0} )$ is generically non-zero because $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$. So, intuitively, if $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$ then $\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )$ is very likely to be non-zero. To make this idea rigorous, we need to use the actual definition of genericity (\cref{def: genericite}), that relies on the coefficients $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}$. Hence we will use the inductive definition of the $c^{-\leftarrow+}$ in terms of the $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}$.\\
Let us prove $\mathcal{P}$ by induction on $p\in \mathbb{P}$. The case $p=0$ is trivial because we have $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } =0$ by \cref{coefs cme non nuls}. Now we assume $p>0$. Let us assume $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$ and prove that $\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero. By~definition of $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ in \cref{eq: def cme}, we are in one of the two following cases.
\begin{itemize}
	\item \underline{Case 1: $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } \neq 0$.\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} By~\cref{coefs cfinal non nuls}, we have $p\in \mathbb{P}+2\tau$ and $p+d-d'\in \mathbb{N}$. By~assumption, we also have $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\subset \mathbb{P}$. Therefore, $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ appears in the right-hand side of \cref{eq: rappel ME de condition de coin CL} (with $p':=\ell ':=0$), which we recall here:
	\begin{equation*}            
		\sigma _{d} (u_{p,\ell } ) = \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P}\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+ \frac{2\pi }{\Theta } }} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ). \tag*{\cref{eq: rappel ME de condition de coin CL}}
	\end{equation*}
	In this expression, $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ is multiplied by $\sigma _{d'} (u^0_{0,0} )$, which is generically non-zero by \cref{def: genericite} because $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$. The coefficient $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ itself is also generically non-zero by \cref{generiqmt non nul ou tjs nul} because of it~is non-zero (for the current value of $\mu _{0} ,\mu _{1} ,\rho _{0} $, etc.). Hence, by \cref{def: genericite}, $\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero.
	\item \underline{Case 2.\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Otherwise, the expression of $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ written in \cref{eq: def cme} contains a non-zero term of the form $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }\cdot c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',p_{2} ,\ell _{2} }$. By~induction hypothesis, $\sigma _{d''} (u^0_{p_{2} ,\ell _{2} })$ is generically non-zero. Using again \cref{eq: rappel ME de condition de coin CL} (this time with $p':=p_{2}$ and $\ell ':=\ell _{2}$) and \cref{def: genericite}, one can verify similarly that $\sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } )$ is generically non-zero.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end demo-117 -->
<!-- demo-118: body_md -->
Let $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$ and $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^* \cap (0,d+m)$. By~\cref{def: mme,eq: sigma de sclDA}, and using \cref{coefs cme non nuls wrt l} to drop the condition $\ell \leqslant \ell _{p}$ in the definition of $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon }$, we have
\begin{align*}
	c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) &= \bigg(\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \, \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } \bigg) \bigg(\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p,\ell } ) \bigg) \\
	&= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,2m)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell }  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} )  \\
	&= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,\textcolor{red!93!black}{m]}} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) +  O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (\epsilon ^{m} )
\end{align*}
where $O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (x)$ denotes a quantity $y$ s.t.\ $|y|\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,x$. Summing over $d'$, we obtain
\begin{multline*}
	\smash{\sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\in (0,d+m)}} \!\! c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon})} = \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m]} \! A_{p} +  O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (\epsilon ^{m} ) \\
	\text{with}  \quad  A_{p} :=\sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)\\ p-p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\in (0,d+m)}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} .
\end{multline*}
By~\cref{ansatz sur Aeps,coefs cme non nuls}, the non-zero terms of $A_{p}$ satisfy $p-p'\in \mathbb{P}+2\tau$ and $p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}$. Moreover, we have $\textstyle \{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^* \mid p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}\} \subset  \tau\mathbb{N}^* \cap [-p',p-p'+d] \subset  (0,d+m)$. We deduce
\[\forall p\in [0,m], \qquad  A_{p} =\sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)\\ p-p'\in (\mathbb{P}+2\tau) \cap [0,m)}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,p+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \! \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p-p',\ell -\ell '} .\]
In addition, when $p<m$, the conditions $p'\in [0,m)$ and $p-p'\in [0,m)$ are~not necessary. Using \cref{condition de coin CL iteree} and then \cref{eq: sigma de sclDA}, we deduce
\[\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,\textcolor{red!93!black}{m)}} A_{p} \, = \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \sigma _{d} (u^0_{p,\ell } ) \,=\, \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}).\]
Hence, it only remains to prove that $A_{m} = O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} )$. When $p=m$, the condition $(p'<m \text{ and } p-p'<m)$ is equivalent to $(p'>0 \text{ and } p-p'>0)$, so:
\begin{align*}
	A_{m} &= \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \mathbb{P} \setminus \{0\}\\ m-p'\in \mathbb{P} +2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,m+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',m-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} ) \\
	&= \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\!\! \sum _{\substack{p'\in \textcolor{red!93!black}{\mathbb{P}}\\ m-p'\in \mathbb{P} +2\tau}} \; \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ p'+d'\in [\![0,m+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',m-p',\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{p',\ell '} )\\
	& \quad \  - \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\! \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\in [\![0,m+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\textcolor{red!93!black}{m},\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{\textcolor{red!93!black}{0},\ell '} ) \\
	&= \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \epsilon \cdot \sigma _{d} (u^0_{m,\ell } ) \,-\, \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\! \sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\in [\![0,m+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} \sum _{\ell '=0} ^{\ell } c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',m,\ell -\ell '} \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{0,\ell '} )
\end{align*}
where we added and substracted the term with $p'=0$, and then used \cref{condition de coin CL iteree}. According to \cref{ansatz sur Aeps,coefs cme non nuls wrt l}, only the terms with $\ell \leqslant \ell _{m}$ in the left sum, and with $\ell '=0$ and $\ell -\ell '\leqslant \ell _{m}$ in the right one, are non-zero. Thus
\[A_{m} \,=\, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\textcolor{red!93!black}{\ell _{m} }} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \epsilon \cdot \sigma _{d} (u^0_{m,\ell } ) \,-\, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\textcolor{red!93!black}{\ell _{m} }} \epsilon ^{m} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \cdot  \!\! \smash{\sum _{\substack{d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\\ d'\in [\![0,m+d]\!]_{\mathbb{P}\!,\mathbb{N}}}} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',m,\ell } \cdot  \sigma _{d'} (u^0_{0,0} )} \,=\, O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} ).\]
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end demo-118 -->
<!-- demo-119: body_md -->
\def\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}{\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}} 
\def\tau{\tau} 
For~any $f\in H^{1} _{\mathrm{loc}} (\Omega )$ and $(r,\theta )$, let us denote $|f|_{r,\theta } := |f(r,\theta )|+r|\nabla  f(r,\theta )|$. We also denote $\tau:= \pi /\Theta $ for simplicity, and
\[\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} := \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \sigma _{n\tau} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -  \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ -m\leqslant d\leqslant N\tau}} \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} .\]
Given \cref{decompo modale SE 1}, it suffices to prove
\[|\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}(r,\theta )|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R,M} \, \frac{\epsilon ^{m} }{r^{m-\tau}} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1} .\]
By~\cref{def: mme}, we have
\begin{align*}
	\sum _{n=1} ^{N} \sigma _{n\tau} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} &= \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \sigma _{n\tau} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n\tau} \,+\, \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \sigma _{n\tau} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \! \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ n\tau-m<d<0}} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,n\tau,\epsilon } \cdot  \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} \\
	&= \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap [0,N\tau]} \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} + \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ d<0}} \Bigg( \underbrace{\sum _{\substack{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap [0,N\tau]\\ d'<d+m}} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) }_{\displaystyle =:A_{d} } \Bigg) \cdot  \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d}
\end{align*}
Let $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$. We have $(d'<d+m \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  d'<m\leqslant N\tau)$ because we assumed $N\geqslant m/\tau$. So \cref{condition de coin sur scl et cme_eps} shows
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: decompo modale SE 2 preuve 1}}
	A_{d} = \sum _{d'\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (0,d+m)} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } \cdot \sigma _{d'} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \,=\, \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) +O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} )
\end{equation}
where $O_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} (x)$ denotes a quantity $y$ s.t.\ $|y|\leqslant C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \, x$. In addition, if $A_{d} \neq 0$, then there exists $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$ s.t.\ $d'<d+m$, so we must have $d>-m+\tau$. We deduce
\begin{align*}
	|\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}(r,\theta )|_{r,\theta } &= \Bigg|\sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (\textcolor{red!93!black}{-m+\tau},0)} \big(A_{d} - \sigma _{d} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \big) \cdot  \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} \Bigg|_{r,\theta } \\
	                                                                                                                                                             
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m+\tau,0)} |\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} |_{r,\theta } \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m+\tau,0)} \sum _{n=0} ^{\min (m-1,\lfloor {d+m}\rfloor )} \epsilon ^{n} \,|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} |_{r,\theta } \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m+\tau,0)} \sum _{n=0} ^{\lfloor {d+m}\rfloor } \epsilon ^{n} \cdot C_{d,n,R} \, r^{d-n} \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} \ \ \text{by \cref{estimation des mcl} }  (r\leqslant R)\\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R,M} \cdot  \epsilon ^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \cdot  r^{-m+\tau} \langle \ln r\rangle^{2m+1} 
\end{align*}
<!-- end demo-119 -->
<!-- demo-120: body_md -->
We recall that, by \cref{def: mme,eq: def cme}, the modes $\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n}$ depends on the coefficients $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell }$, which are defined using the coefficients $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$. Let us express these objects one after another, beginning with $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$. We mainly use the results of \cref{sec: simplifications DA} and its extension Appendix~\ref{sec: annexe simplifications DA cas rationnel}.\smallskip

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} If $\tau \in \mathbb{Q}$, let us denote $b$ the denominator of $\frac{\Theta }{\pi }$ in irreducible form (i.e.\ $\Theta  = \frac{a\pi }{b}$ with $a\in \mathbb{N}$ and $\gcd(a,b)=1$). Otherwise, we define $b:=+\infty $. Let $(d,d',p,\ell )\in (-\tau\mathbb{N}^*)\times \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\times \mathbb{P}\times \mathbb{N}$ be s.t.
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve hyp sur p}}
	\textstyle  p<m \, \text{ and } \, (d'\in -\mathbb{N} \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  p<b+\tau).
\end{equation}
Let us show:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal}}
	c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell } = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
	\omega ^{2k} \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d',k} ) & \text{if $d'>0$, $\ell =0$ and there exists $k\in \mathbb{N}$ s.t.\ }  p=d'-d+2k\\
	0 & \text{otherwise}.
	\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
There are several cases, given that we assumed $\Theta  \not\in E_{m}$.
\begin{enumerate}
	\item If $\tau \not\in \mathbb{Q}$, then \cref{valeur de cmaicro cas irrationnel} shows \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal} (unconditionally on $p$ in fact).
	\item Let us assume $\tau \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $b\not\in F_{m}$, with $F_{3} :=\{1\}$ and $F_{5} :=\{1,3\}$. Let us use the notation $\beta $ from \cref{sec: annexe simplifications DA cas rationnel}, which is an integer s.t.\ for any $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$ and $n<\beta $, $\Phi^0_{d,n}$ can be expressed with Bessel functions (more details in \cref{sec: annexe simplifications DA cas rationnel}). \Cref{valeur de cfinal cas rationnel generalise} shows \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal} for~any $p$ s.t.
	\begin{equation}{\label{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal bis}}
		\textstyle p<\min (\beta ,2b+2\tau) \, \text{ and } \, (d'\in -\mathbb{N} \mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  p<b+\tau),
	\end{equation}
	Let us check that \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal bis} is satisfied. Given the assumption \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve hyp sur p}, it suffices to prove $\min (\beta ,2b+2\tau)\geqslant m$, i.e. $\beta \geqslant m$ and $2b+2\tau\geqslant m$. Propositions~\ref{expression sing heterog CL} and \ref{expression sing heterog CL avec BesselY} show that we have $\beta \geqslant b$, which yields $\beta \geqslant m$ when $b\geqslant m$. Otherwise, we have $b\in [\![1,m-1]\!] \setminus F_{m} \subset  \{2,4\}$ and \cref{expression sing heterog CL b=2 ou 4} shows $\beta \geqslant 5\geqslant m$. In addition, we have $b\geqslant 2$ and $\tau\geqslant  \frac{1}{2}$, so $2b+2\tau\geqslant 5$. Therefore \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal bis} holds, which implies \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal}.
	\item The only remaining case is ($\Theta  = \frac{\pi }{3}$ and $m=5$). By~\cref{coefs cfinal non nuls}, $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ vanishes when $p<2\tau=6$. The right-hand side of \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal} also vanishes when $p<2\tau$. This proves \cref{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cfinal} in this case.
\end{enumerate}
\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us show a similar expression for the coefficients $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell }$: for any $(d,d',p,\ell )\in (-\tau\mathbb{N}^*)\times \tau\mathbb{N}^*\times \mathbb{P}\times \mathbb{N}$ s.t.\ $p<m$, we have
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: expression mme sauf cas speciaux preuve cme}}
	c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
	\omega ^{2k} \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{d',k} ) & \text{if $\ell =0$ and there exists $k\in \mathbb{N}$ s.t.\ }  p=d'-d+2k\\
	0 & \text{otherwise}.
	\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
By~\cref{eq: def cme}, $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } -c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$ is equal to a sum of terms of the form $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p_{1} ,\ell _{1} } \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d'',d',p_{2} ,\ell _{2} }$ with $p_{1} +p_{2} =p$, $p_{1} <p$, $d''<0$ and $d'' \geqslant d'-p_{2}$. If $d''\not\in -\mathbb{N}$, then step~1 shows that we have $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }=0$ because $p_{1} <m$. Otherwise, we have $p_{2} \geqslant d'-d''\geqslant \tau+b$, which implies $p_{1} =p-p_{2} <m-(b+\tau) \leqslant b+\tau$ (because $2(b+\tau)\geqslant 2(2+ \frac{1}{2} )\geqslant m$). So we can also apply step~1, which gives again  $c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d'',p_{1} ,\ell _{1} }=0$. Hence we have $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } =c^{\mathbf{u}\leftarrow\mathbf{u}}_{d,d',p,\ell }$. We conclude using step~1 one more time.\medskip

\underline{Step 3:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} According to \cref{def: mme}, step~2 implies for any $d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*$ and $d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$:\vspace{-1ex}
\[c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } := \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell _{p}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } = \sum _{k\in \mathbb{N},\,n\tau-d+2k<m} \! \epsilon ^{n\tau-d+2k} \, \omega ^{2k} \, \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{n\tau,k} ),\]
which yields ${\displaystyle \use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} := \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n\tau} + \; \sum _{\substack{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\\ \mathclap{n\tau-m<d<0}}} \; c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,n\tau,\epsilon } \cdot  \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} =\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n\tau} + \!\! \sum _{\substack{d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*,\, k\in \mathbb{N}\\|d|+2k<m-n\tau}} \! \epsilon ^{n\tau-d+2k} \, \omega ^{2k} \, \sigma _{d} (\mathcal{S}^\infty_{n\tau,k} ) \cdot \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} }$.
<!-- end demo-120 -->
<!-- demo-121: body_md -->
In both cases, $\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}(u,u)$ has the form $x-\omega ^2 y$ with $x,y\in \mathbb{R}_+$ that depend on $u$. It suffices to notice that we have $\Im( \overline{\omega }(x-\omega ^2 y))=\Im( \overline{\omega }x-\omega |\omega |^2  y)=\Im( \overline{\omega })(x+|\omega |^2 y)$ with $|\omega |^2 >0$.
<!-- end demo-121 -->
<!-- demo-122: body_md -->
To begin, let us show that, for~any $d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$ and $r>0$, we have $J_{d} (k_{0} r) \neq 0$. It is a known property of Bessel functions that all the zeros of $J_{a}$ are real, but it~is easy and interesting to prove in this context.
\begin{sousdemo}
	Let us assume by contradiction that there exist $d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$ and $r_{1} >0$ s.t.\ $J_{d} (k_{0} r_{1} ) =0$. Let $f:(r,\theta ) \mapsto  J_{d} (k_{0} r)\sin (d\theta )$ be defined on $D:=\Omega  \cap B(0,r_{1} )$. By~assumption, we have $f_{|\partial D} =0$. By~properties of the Bessel functions, we also have $\Delta f-k_{0} ^2 f=0$ (see \cite{Leb72} and the proof of \cref{relations sur BesselGamma/Omega}). Moreover, we have $f\in H^{1} (D)$ because $J_{d} (k_{0} r)=O(r^{d} )$ when $r\rightarrow 0$ by \cite{Leb72}. Now, Helmholtz's problem with Dirichlet condition is well-posed in $H^{1} _{0} (D)$ because $\Im(\omega ) \neq 0$ (see e.g.\ \cref{pb de Helmholtz variationnel}). Thus $f=0$ in $D$, which is absurd.
\end{sousdemo}
Next, for~any $d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$, let $f_{d} :r\in \mathbb{R}_+^*\mapsto \big|\Gamma (d+1) \big( \frac{2}{k_{0} \textcolor{red!93!black}{r}} \big)^{d} J_{d} (k_{0} r)\big|$. We need to prove $\smash{\inf\limits _{d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\!,\,r\in (0,R]} f_{d} }>0$. \cite[p.\,44]{Wat95} states:
\begin{equation}{\label{estimation de Wat95 pour ME}}
	\forall q\in \mathbb{R}_+,\ \forall z\in \mathbb{C}^*, \qquad  \left| \Gamma (q+1) \left( \frac{2}{z} \right)^{q} J_{q} (z) - 1 \right| \leqslant  \exp \!\left( \frac{|z|^2 }{4(q+1)} \right) -1.
\end{equation}
Let $d_{0} \in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$ be s.t.\ $\exp \!\big( \frac{R^2 }{4(d_{0} +1)}\big)-1\leqslant  \frac{1}{2}$. Then we have $ \frac{1}{2} \leqslant  f_{d} (r) \leqslant  \frac{3}{2}$ for~any $d\geqslant d_{0}$ and $r\in (0,R]$. Moreover, for any $d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*$ s.t.\ $d<d_{0}$, we have $f_{d} (r)\rightarrow 1$ when $r\rightarrow 0^{+}$ by \cite{Leb72}, and $f_{d}$ has no zero in $(0,R]$ by the beginning of this proof. Hence $f_{d}$ can be extended into a positive continuous function on $[0,R]$. By~compacity, we deduce $\min _{d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\!,d<d_{0} } \inf _{(0,R]} f_{d} >0$ and $\max _{d\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*\!,d<d_{0} } \sup _{(0,R]} f_{d} <\infty $ which concludes the proof.
<!-- end demo-122 -->
<!-- demo-123: body_md -->
By~\cref{eq: mme qd eps=0}, each $\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n}$ is equal to $\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0}$ and is proportional on $\Sigma^\circ$ to $J_{d} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}) \sin (d\theta )$ with $d:=n\tau$. The functions $\theta \mapsto \sin (d\theta )$ are orthogonal between each other and the $J_{d} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})$ do~not vanish by \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ}, so $\use@eps{G_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0$ is a diagonal inversible matrix. Hence we have: $\forall v\in L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\;\forall \mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^\circ,$
\begin{align}
	\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v)(\mathbf{x})                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
	&= \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \langle v,\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0} \rangle  \cdot  \|\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^{-2} \cdot  \partial _{r} \Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0} (\mathbf{x}) \nonumber\\
	&= \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \langle v,f _{n} \rangle  \, \partial _{r} f _{n} (\mathbf{x}) \quad\qquad  \text{with }  f _{n} := \frac{\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} }{\|\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} }
	\label{eq: opS positif qd eps=0 preuve expression opSref}
\end{align}
Let $w:\Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be defined by $w := \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \langle v,f _{n} \rangle  \, f _{n} $. We have shown that $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v) =\partial _{r} w_{|\Sigma^\circ}$. Let $V :=\operatorname{Span}(f _{1|\Sigma^\circ} ,\dots ,f _{N|\Sigma^\circ} ) \subset L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$. Using again \cref{eq: mme qd eps=0}, we know that $f _{n|\Sigma^\circ}$ and $\partial _{r} f _{n|\Sigma^\circ}$ are both proportional to $\sin (n\tau \theta )$, so they are colinear in $L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$. This yields $\partial _{r} w\in V$. Moreover, $(f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} )_{n}$ is an orthonormal family, so $w_{|\Sigma^\circ}$ is the $L^2 $ orthogonal projection of $v$ on $V$. We deduce $\langle \partial _{r} w, v-w\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} =0$. Therefore, we obtain:
\[\langle \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v),v\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} = \langle \partial _{r} w, v\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} = \langle \partial _{r} w, w\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} = \int _{\Omega \cap B(0,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})} \big(|\nabla  w|^2 -k_{0} ^2 |w|^2 \big)\]
because \cref{convergence des mcl} implies that $w$ satisfies $\Delta w+k_{0} ^2 w=0$ in $\Omega $ and $w=0$ on $\partial \Omega $. We conclude as in the proof of \cref{coercivite partie hors DtN des ME}, by noticing that $\langle \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v),v\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$ has the form $x-\omega ^2 y$ with $x,y\in \mathbb{R}_+$ and that $\Im( \overline{\omega })\,\Im( \overline{\omega }(x-\omega ^2 y))=\Im( \overline{\omega })^2 (x+|\omega |^2 y)\geqslant 0$.
<!-- end demo-123 -->
<!-- demo-124: body_md -->
Let $d:=n\tau$. \Cref{def: mcle,expression sing homog CL} shows that we have $\Phi^{N}_{d,0} = (-1)^{n} \,\Gamma (d+1) \.\big( \frac{2}{k_{0}} \big)^{d} J_{d} (k_{0} r) \sin (d\theta )$. With \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ}, this directly implies $\|\Phi^{N}_{d,0} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant C_{R} \,(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{n\tau}$. Moreover, we have $2 J_{d} '(z) = J_{d-1} (z)-J_{d+1} (z)$ by \cite{Leb72}. Using again \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ}, we get $|\Gamma (d+1) \big( \frac{2}{k_{0}} \big)^{d} J_{d} '(k_{0} r)| \leqslant  C_{R} \,d\.r^{d-1}$. Since $\partial _{r} \Phi^{N}_{d,0} = (-1)^{n} \,\Gamma (d+1) \big( \frac{2}{k_{0}} \big)^{d} k_{0} J_{d} '(k_{0} r) \sin (d\theta )$, we deduce $\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} \Phi^{N}_{d,0} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{R} \,d^{j+1} \*\.(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{n\tau-1}$.
<!-- end demo-124 -->
<!-- demo-125: body_md -->
We recall that, according to \cref{estimation des mcl}, we have for any $\delta \in \mathbb{R}$, $d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*$ s.t.\ $d\geqslant \delta $, $n\in \mathbb{N}$, $s>1$, $r\in (0,R]$ and $\theta \in [0,\Theta ]$:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: estimation mme preuve 1}}
	|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} (r,\theta )| + r|\nabla  \Phi^{N}_{d,n} (r,\theta )| \leqslant  C_{\delta ,n,R,s} \,(s r)^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} .
\end{equation}
It is not difficult to extend this result to higher order derivatives and show:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: estimation mme preuve 1 generalise}}
	\forall (i,j)\in \mathbb{N}^2 ,\qquad  r^{i+j} |\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} \Phi^{N}_{d,n} (r,\theta )| \leqslant  C_{\delta ,n,R,s,i,j} \,(s r)^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1} .
\end{equation}
This requires to modify \cref{majoration des fonctions de A par leur norme,cvg des SF de norme finie,convergence des mcl} to control the derivatives of high order in the same way we controlled the first derivative. Each derivation introduces an additional factor $1/r$ in the bound, which explains the factors $r$ in \cref{eq: estimation mme preuve 1} and $r^{i+j}$ in \cref{eq: estimation mme preuve 1 generalise}. Next, for any $f\in H^{3} _{\mathrm{loc}} (\Omega )$ and $(r,\theta )$, let us denote
\[|f|_{r,\theta } := |f(r,\theta )|+r|\partial _{r} f(r,\theta )|+r|\partial _{\theta } \partial _{r} f(r,\theta )|+r|\partial _{\theta } ^2  \partial _{r} f(r,\theta )|.\]
Taking $\delta :=-m$, $s :=2$, $d\leqslant N\tau$ and $n\in [\![0,m]\!]$, we obtain in particular $|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} |_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{R,N} \, r^{d-n} \, \langle \ln r\rangle^{2n+1}$. By~\cref{eq: def mse}, this yields for $r:=\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: estimation mse}}
	\big|\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} \big|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  \sum _{n=0} ^{m-1} \epsilon ^{n} \big|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} \big|_{r,\theta } 
	\leqslant  \sum _{n=0} ^{m-1} C_{R,N} \, r^{d} \left( \frac{\epsilon \,\langle \ln r\rangle^2 }{r} \right)^{n} \langle \ln r\rangle
	\leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \, r^{d} \,\langle \ln r\rangle
\end{equation}
because $\epsilon \,\langle \ln r\rangle^2  \leqslant  Mr$ by assumption. Similarly, we have 
\[\big|\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} -\Phi^{N}_{d,0} \big|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  \sum _{n=\textcolor{red!93!black}{1}} ^{m-1} C_{R,N} \, r^{d} \left( \frac{\epsilon \,\langle \ln r\rangle^2 }{r} \right)^{n} \langle \ln r\rangle \leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \, \epsilon \, r^{d-1} \,\langle \ln r\rangle^{3} .\]
Now, in order to bound the modes $\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n}$, which involve the coefficients $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon }$, let us show: ${\forall d\in -\tau\mathbb{N}^*},\allowbreak\, \forall d'\in \tau\mathbb{N}^*,\; |c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } | \leqslant  C_{R,M,d,d'} \,\epsilon ^{d'-d} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3(d'-d-1)}$.
\begin{sousdemo}
	\defq{q} 
	Let $q:= d'-d$. By~\cref{def: mme,coefs cme non nuls}, we have
	\[c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } := \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap [0,m)} \, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell _{p}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } = \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P} \cap \textcolor{red!93!black}{[q,m)}} \, \sum _{\ell =0} ^{\ell _{p}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon  \cdot  c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',p,\ell } .\]
	If $q\geqslant m$, this yields $c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } =0$. Let us assume $q<m$. Since $\epsilon \leqslant Mr\leqslant MR$, we deduce $|c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,d',\epsilon } |\leqslant  C_{R,M,d,d'} \,\epsilon ^{q} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{q}} $. To conclude, it suffices to prove $\ell _{q} \leqslant 3(q-1)$.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item If $\Theta =\pi $, then we have $q \in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}} \cap [0,5)=[\![0,4]\!]$ so \cref{tab: liste CL pour pi} shows $\ell _{q} \leqslant  q -1$. In addition, we have $q\geqslant 2\tau\geqslant 1$, so we deduce $\ell _{q} \leqslant  3(q-1)$.
		\item Otherwise, we have $\ell _{q} \leqslant \ell _{m} \leqslant 1$ by \cref{rq: degre en ln eps dans ME} and, if $q<2$, then $\ell _{q} =0$ by \cref{simplifications cas irrationnel,simplifications cas rationnel}. Since $q\geqslant 2\tau\geqslant 1$, this implies $\ell _{q} \leqslant 3(q-1)$.
	\end{itemize}
\end{sousdemo}
Let us also show that we have $\epsilon \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3} \leqslant  C_{R,M} \.r$ (still with $r:=\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$).
\begin{itemize}
	\item If $\epsilon \leqslant r^2 $, then we have $\epsilon \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3} \leqslant  C_{R,M} \sqrt{\epsilon } \leqslant C_{R,M} \.r$ because $\epsilon \leqslant Mr\leqslant M R$.
	\item Otherwise, we have $\epsilon \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3} \leqslant  \epsilon  \cdot C \langle \ln r\rangle^{3} \leqslant C_{M} \.r$. 
\end{itemize}
Recalling that $\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} =\Phi^{N}_{n\tau,0}$ by~\cref{eq: mme qd eps=0}, and using \cref{def: mme}, we deduce
\begin{align*}
	\big|\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} \big|_{r,\theta } &= \bigg|\use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n\tau} -\Phi^{N}_{n\tau,0} + \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m,0)} c^{-\leftarrow+}_{d,n\tau,\epsilon } \cdot  \use@eps{\Phi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{d} \bigg|_{r,\theta } \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \bigg( \epsilon \,r^{n\tau-1} \langle \ln r\rangle ^{3} + \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m,0)} \epsilon ^{n\tau-d} \,\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3(n\tau-d-1)} \cdot  r^{d} \,\langle \ln r\rangle \bigg) \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \,\epsilon \,r^{n\tau-1} \langle \ln r\rangle^{3} \bigg( 1 + \sum _{d\in \@ifstar{\tau\mathbb{Z}^*}{\tau\mathbb{Z}}*\cap (-m,0)} \left( \frac{\epsilon \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3} }{r} \right)^{n\tau-d-1} \bigg) \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \,\epsilon \, r^{n\tau-1} \langle \ln r\rangle^{3}
\end{align*}
using $n\tau-d-1\geqslant 2\tau-1\geqslant 0$ and $\epsilon \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{3} \leqslant  C_{R,M} \.r$. Moreover \cref{estimation mcld0} shows that $|\Phi^{N}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} |_{r,\theta } \leqslant C_{R,N} \,r^{n\pi/\Theta}$. Compared to the previous bound on $|\Phi^{N}_{d,n} |_{r,\theta }$, this one does~not involve $\ln r$, which will slightly improve the powers of $\ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$ (although this is not essential). Thanks to the hypothesis $\epsilon \,\langle \ln r\rangle^{3} \leqslant  Mr$, this yields $\big|\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \big|_{r,\theta } \leqslant \big|\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} \big|_{r,\theta } +\big|\Phi^{N}_{n\tau,0} \big|_{r,\theta } \leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \,r^{n\tau} $.
<!-- end demo-125 -->
<!-- demo-126: body_md -->
Let us introduce the following normalized variables:
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\forall n\in [\![1,N]\!],\ a_{n} :=\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\Theta /2} \cdot  {\Gamma (n\tau+1)}\* \big( \frac{2}{k_{0}} \big)^{n\pi/\Theta} J_{n\pi/\Theta} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})$, which is non-zero by \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ},
	\item $\forall n\in [\![1,N]\!],\ \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} :=\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} /a_{n}$,
	\item $\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}} :=\big[\langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \big]_{(n,n')\in [\![1,N]\!]^2 }$,
	\item $D = \mathrm{Diag} \big[a_{1} ,\dots ,a_{N} \big]\in \mathrm{GL}_{N} (\mathbb{C})$.
\end{itemize}
$\use@eps{G_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ is invertible iff $\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}} = D^{-1} \use@eps{G_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}} D^{-1}$ is invertible, and in this case we have: $\forall v\in L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\;\forall \mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^\circ,$
\begin{align}
	\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(v)(\mathbf{x}) &= \Big[\langle v ,\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \Big]_{n} ^{\mathsf{T}} D^{-1} \cdot (D^{-1} \use@eps{G_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}} D^{-1} )^{-1} \cdot  D^{-1} \Big[\partial _{r} \use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} (\mathbf{x})\Big]_{n} \nonumber\\[.5ex]
	&= \Big[\langle v ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \Big]_{n} ^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot  \use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \cdot \Big[\partial _{r} \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} (\mathbf{x})\Big]_{n} . \label{eq: opS - opS0 preuve expression opS normalisee}
\end{align}
Moreover \cref{eq: mme qd eps=0} shows that we have for~any $n\in [\![1,N]\!]$: $\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n|\Sigma^\circ} = \Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0|\Sigma^\circ} = (-1)^{n} \,a_{n} \sqrt{ \frac{2}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\Theta } } \*\sin (n\tau \theta )$. Since the functions $\sqrt{ \frac{2}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\Theta } } \sin (n\tau \theta )$ are orthonormal in $L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$, we deduce
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: opS - opS0 preuve gram normalisee eps=0}}
	\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0 = \bigg[\Big\langle  \frac{1}{a_{n}} \Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0} ,\, \frac{1}{a_{n'}} \Phi^{\rm lim}_{n'\tau,0} \Big\rangle _{\!L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \bigg]_{n,n'} = I_{N} .
\end{equation}

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} We will prove that $\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ is invertible for small values of $\epsilon $ using the Neumann series ``$\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} =(I_{N} -(\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}))^{-1} =\sum_{j=0}^\infty  (\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}})^{j}$''. To begin, \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ} implies $|a_{n} |\geqslant C_{R} \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{n\tau}$. Therefore, \cref{estimation mme} used with $M:=1$ implies that, for any $j\in \{0,1,2\}$, if $\epsilon \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \leqslant \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$ then:
 
	\def\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}#$}\endgroup$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}${\begingroup
		\setbox0=\hbox{$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$} 
		\ifmmode\hbox to \wd0{$#$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$$\hss} 
		\else\hbox to \wd0{#$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$\hss}\fi\endgroup} 
	\def\ralignbox#$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}${\begingroup
		\setbox0=\hbox{$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$} 
		\ifmmode\hbox to \wd0{\hss$#$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$$} 
		\else\hbox to \wd0{\hss #$\|\partial _{\theta ^{j}} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$}\fi\endgroup}
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{-1/2}$,
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{-3/2}$,
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{-3/2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$,
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} (\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} )\|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)}$}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})^{-5/2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$.
\end{itemize}
Besides, we have
\begin{align*}
	\langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} &= \langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle  + \langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle  \\
	&= \langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n'} \rangle  + \langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n'} \rangle  + \langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\,\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle  \vspace{-1ex}
\end{align*}
Hence
\begin{align*}
	|\langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \rangle _{L^2 } -\langle \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} ,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n'} \rangle _{L^2 } | &\leqslant  \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \, \|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)} \|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n'} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	& \qquad  {}+ \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \, \|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} -\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0_{n} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)} \|\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n'} \|_{L^{\infty } (\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N,M} \,\epsilon \, \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}
\end{align*}
Next, we introduce the following norms for any $(z_{n} )\in \mathbb{C}^{N}$ and $A\in \mathcal{M}_{N} (\mathbb{C})$:
\[\|(z_{n} )\|_{\infty } :=\max (|z_{1} |,\dots ,|z_{N} |) \qquad  \text{ and } \qquad  \|A\|_{\infty } := \sup _{\mathbf z\in \mathbb{C}^{N} \setminus \{0\}} \frac{\|A\bf z\|_{\infty } }{\|\bf z\|_{\infty } }.\]
For~any $A=\big[a_{i,j} \big]\in \mathcal{M}_{N} (\mathbb{C})$, we have $\|A\|_{\infty } =\max _{i\in [\![1,N]\!]} \sum _{j=1} ^{N} |a_{i,j} |$. Hence we have $\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0\|_{\infty } \leqslant  C^{\mathrm{gram}} _{R,N} \,\epsilon \, \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$ for some constant $C^{\mathrm{gram}} _{R,N} >0$, provided that $\epsilon \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \leqslant \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$. Now let us define $C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} := \min (1, \frac{1}{2} (C^{\mathrm{gram}} _{R,N} )^{-1} )$. Then for any $\epsilon  \leqslant  C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$ we have $\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0\|_{\infty } \leqslant  \frac{1}{2}$, which implies that $\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ is invertible and
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\displaystyle \|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \|_{\infty } \leqslant  \sum\limits_{j=0}^\infty  \|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0\|_{\infty } ^{j} \leqslant  2$\vspace{-0.5ex}
	\item $\displaystyle \|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} -\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0^{-1} \|_{\infty } \leqslant  \sum\limits_{j=1}^\infty  \|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0\|_{\infty } ^{j} \leqslant  2\,C^{\mathrm{gram}} _{R,N,M} \, \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{4} = C_{R,N} \, \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$.
\end{itemize}
\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} It remains to estimate the operator norms of $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$, $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}$ and $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$. Let us assume $\epsilon  \leqslant  C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R,N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \*\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$. Let $v\in L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$ and $\mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^\circ$. We define $V_{\epsilon } (v):=\big[\langle v,\use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \rangle \big]_{n} \in \mathbb{C}^{N}$ and $V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x}):=\big[\partial _{r} \use@eps{\widetilde{\Psi}^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} (\mathbf{x})\big]_{n} \in \mathbb{C}^{N}$. Step 1 provides the following estimates (taking $M:=1$ and $j\in \{0,1,2\}$):
 
	\def\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}#$}\endgroup$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }${\begingroup
		\setbox0=\hbox{$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$} 
		\ifmmode\hbox to \wd0{$#$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$$\hss} 
		\else\hbox to \wd0{#$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$\hss}\fi\endgroup} 
	\def\ralignbox#$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }${\begingroup
		\setbox0=\hbox{$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$} 
		\ifmmode\hbox to \wd0{\hss$#$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$$} 
		\else\hbox to \wd0{\hss #$\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty }$}\fi\endgroup}
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|V_{\epsilon } (v)\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|V_{\epsilon } (v)-V_{0} (v)\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-3/2} $
	\item $\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup \leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-5/2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$
\end{itemize}
\Cref{eq: opS - opS0 preuve expression opS normalisee} shows that $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(v)(\mathbf{x})=V_{\epsilon } (v)^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot \use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \cdot V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x})$. Hence we~have
\def\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth

	\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|(\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
	\dimen0=\linewidth
	\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0

	\hbox to \dimen0{${}#1$}\endgroup}
\begin{align*}
	\big|(\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big| &\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth

	&\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\hfill {}+ V_{0} (v)^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot \use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0^{-1} \cdot (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\big|$}\endgroup\\
	&\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\leqslant  N\, \|V_{\epsilon } (v)-V_{0} (v)\|_{\infty } \,\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \|_{\infty } \,\|V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } \hfill$}\endgroup\\
	&\begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\hfill {} + N\, \|V_{0} (v)\|_{\infty } \,\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} -\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0^{-1} \|_{\infty } \,\|V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup\\
	& \begingroup
			\setbox0=\hbox{$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$}
			\dimen0=\linewidth
			\advance\dimen0 by -\wd0
			\advance\dimen0 by -4.5em
			\hbox to \dimen0{${}\hfill {} + N\, \|V_{0} (v)\|_{\infty } \,\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}0^{-1} \|_{\infty } \,\|V'_{\epsilon } (\mathbf{x})-V'_{0} (\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } $}\endgroup\\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-5/2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}
\end{align*}
$\big|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)(\mathbf{x})\big|$ can be bounded in the same way. Thus $\big\|(\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}})(v)\big\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{R,N} \*\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$.\\
As for $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$, we have $V'_{0} (P^\circ)=\big[\partial _{r} \Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0} (P^\circ)\big]_{n}$ by \cref{eq: mme qd eps=0}. Since $\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\tau,0|\partial \Omega } =0$ by \cref{convergence des mcl}, we get $V'_{0} (P^\circ) =0$. Therefore:\vspace{-.5ex}
\begin{align*}
	|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(v)| &= \big|V_{\epsilon } (v)^{\mathsf{T}} \cdot \use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \cdot (V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\big| \\
	&\leqslant  N\, \|V_{\epsilon } (v)\|_{\infty } \,\|\use@eps{\widetilde{G}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}^{-1} \|_{\infty } \,\|(V'_{\epsilon } -V'_{0} )(\mathbf{x})\|_{\infty } \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R,N} \,\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-5/2} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} .
\end{align*}
