<!-- demo-127: body_md -->
\defC_{\rm coer}{C_{\rm coer}} 
\def\ell_\omega{\ell_\omega}                                 
\defb^{(#)}_01{b^{(#1)}_0} 
\defc^{(#)}_\epsilon1{c^{(#1)}_\epsilon} 
\defc^{(m)}_\epsilon{c^{(m)}_\epsilon} 
Let $\ell_\omega:z\in \mathbb{C}\mapsto \Im( \overline{\omega })\,\Im( \overline{\omega }z)$. We define the following norms
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: norme VME}}
	\left\{\begin{array}{l}
	\forall u\in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3, \quad  \|u\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3,\epsilon } := \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \\
	\forall u\in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5, \quad  \|u\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5,\epsilon } := \big( \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2  + \epsilon  \,\lvertu\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)}^2  \big)^{1/2} 
	\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
\Cref{coercivite partie hors DtN des ME} states that there exists $C_{\rm coer}>0$ s.t.: $\forall u\in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}},\; \ell_\omega(\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}(u,u))\geqslant  C_{\rm coer} \|u\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}},\epsilon }$. We will prove that, for an appropriate choice of $C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N}$, $\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}$ is also coercive for $\|.\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}},\epsilon }$, with constant $C_{\rm coer}/2$.\\
Let $c^{(m)}_\epsilon:=\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon} -b^{(m)}_0$. We recall that, by \cref{opS - opS0}, there exists $C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} , C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 2}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} >0$ s.t., for~any $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\in (0,R_{\mathrm{s}})$ and $\epsilon \leqslant C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$, $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ and $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ are well defined and 
\[\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ))} + \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\mathbb{C})} \leqslant   C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 2}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \, \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{2}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} .\]

\underline{Case $m=3$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} For~any $u\in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3$ we have:
\[|c^{(3)}_\epsilon(u,u)| = \big|\big\langle \mu _{0} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}3-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}3)(u_{|\Sigma^\circ} ),u \big\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \big| \leqslant  \mu _{0} \.C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 2}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \, \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{2}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|u\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  .\]
Let us show that we have
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: norme L2 SME vs H1 OME}}
	\|u\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  \leqslant C\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2  . \vspace{-1ex}
\end{equation}
\begin{sousdemo}
	Let $\widetilde{\Omega } :=\Omega  \setminus \overline{B}(0,1)$ and $\widetilde{\Sigma } := \Omega  \cap \partial B(0,1)$. We have $\Omega^\circ =\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \widetilde{\Omega }$ and $\Sigma^\circ=\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \widetilde{\Sigma }$. Let $\tilde{u} \in H^{1} ( \widetilde{\Omega })$ be defined by $\tilde{u}:x \mapsto u(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} x)$. It is easy to see that we have $\|u\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2 =\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \| \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 ( \widetilde{\Sigma })} ^2 $ and $\|\nabla  u\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} ^2 =\|\nabla  \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 ( \widetilde{\Omega })}^2 $. Finally, since $u_{|\Sigma_\Omega^\circ} =0$, Poincaré's inequality gives $\| \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 ( \widetilde{\Sigma })} \leqslant C\|\nabla  \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 ( \widetilde{\Omega })}$.
\end{sousdemo}
Thus we obtain $|c^{(3)}_\epsilon(u,u)| \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \, \epsilon  \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \.\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \.\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} ^2 $.\\
Besides, we have $b^{(3)}_0(u,u)=\langle \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(u_{|\Sigma^\circ} ), u\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$, so \cref{opS positif qd eps=0} shows that $\ell_\omega(b^{(3)}_0(u,u))\geqslant  0$. Therefore:
\defC^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N}{C^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N}}
\begin{align*}
	|\omega |^2 \big|(\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3)(u,u)\big| &\geqslant  \ell_\omega\big((\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3)(u,u)\big)\\
	&\geqslant  \ell_\omega(\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3(u,u)) + \ell_\omega(b^{(3)}_0(u,u)) + \ell_\omega(c^{(3)}_\epsilon(u,u)) \\
	&\geqslant  C_{\rm coer} \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} ^2  + 0 - C^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \, \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} ^2     
	                                                     
\end{align*}
for some constant $C^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N}$. Hence $|\omega |^2 \big|(\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3)(u,u)\big| \geqslant  \frac{C_{\rm coer}}{2} \,\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}$ provided that $C^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \, \epsilon  \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \*\,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \leqslant  C_{\rm coer}/2$. Let us define
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: caractere bien pose des ME augmentes preuve def Cstab m=3}}
	C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N} := \min \left(C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} , \frac{C_{\rm coer}}{2\,C^\star_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} }\right).
\end{equation}
We have proven that, when $\epsilon \leqslant  C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$ (i.e.\ the stability condition of \cref{def: condition de stabilite}), $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ is well defined and $\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}3$ is uniformly coercive w.r.t.\ $(\epsilon ,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},N)$. Moreover, using again \cref{eq: norme L2 SME vs H1 OME}, we have:
\[\forall v\in H^{1} (\Omega^\circ), \qquad  \ell^{(3)}(v) \leqslant  C\,\big(\|\tilde{f}_{\rm s}\|_{H^{-1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \|g_{\rm s}\|_{L^2 (\Gamma^\circ)} + \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \|h_{\rm s}\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \big) \,\|v\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} .\]
Thus Lax-Milgram's theorem implies the well-posedness and uniform stability of \cref{eq: FV ME augmente}.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Case $m=5$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} This is very similar to the previous case, but this time we have
\begin{align}
	|c^{(5)}_\epsilon(u,u)| &= \left|\big\langle \mu _{0} (\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}5)(u_{|\Sigma^\circ} ),u \big\rangle _{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} + \frac{\epsilon \mu _{1} }{3} \,\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5(u_{|\Sigma^\circ} ) \,\overline{u(P^\circ)}\right| \nonumber\\
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \left( \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \, \|u\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  + \frac{\epsilon ^2 }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{5/2}} \,\|u\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)} \right) \nonumber\\
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \left( \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \, \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} ^2  + \frac{\epsilon ^2 }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \,\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)} \right) \nonumber\\
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \left( \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \, \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} ^2  + \frac{\epsilon ^{3/2} }{2\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \,\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2  + \frac{\epsilon ^{3/2} }{2\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \, \epsilon \,\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)}^2  \right) \nonumber\\
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \left( \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} + \frac{\epsilon ^{3/2} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \right) \|u\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5,\epsilon } ^2  \label{eq: caractere bien pose des ME augmentes preuve m=5 forme c}
\end{align}
Now note that, since $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\leqslant R_{\mathrm{s}}$, we have for~any $M>0$:
\begin{align}
	\epsilon \leqslant M \, \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{4/3} }{\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^2 } \quad  &\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  \quad  \epsilon ^{3/2} \leqslant  M^{3/2} \, \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 }{\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}} \; \text{ and } \; \epsilon \leqslant M\,C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}}  \nonumber\\
	&\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  \quad  \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \left( \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} + \frac{\epsilon ^{3/2} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2 } \right) \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,(M+M^{3/2} ). \label{eq: caractere bien pose des ME augmentes preuve m=5 etude condition stab}
\end{align}
Hence, for a sufficiently small value of $C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N}$, the stability condition ``$\epsilon \leqslant C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{4/3} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-2}$'' implies:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\roman*)}]
	\item $\epsilon  \leqslant C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$, so $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5$ and $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5$ are well-defined,
	\item and $|c^{(5)}_\epsilon(u,u)| \leqslant  \frac{C_{\rm coer}}{2} \|u\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5,\epsilon } ^2 $, which implies that $\use@m{a^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}5+\use@m{b^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}5$ is uniformly coercive (same proof as $m=3$). Moreover, it~is easy to see that we have $|\ell^{(5)}(v)| \leqslant  C\,(\|\tilde{f}_{\rm s}\|_{H^{-1}} + \|g_{\rm s}\|_{L^2 } + \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \|h_{\rm s}\|_{L^2 } +\epsilon ^{- \frac{1}{2} }|p_{\rm s}|) \|v\|_{\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5,\epsilon }$ for~any $v\in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}5$. So \cref{eq: FV ME augmente} is again well-posed and uniformly stable.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end demo-127 -->
<!-- paragraphesansboite-21: body_md -->
\label{hyp: Cstab majore} 
Replacing $C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N}$ by $\min (C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N},1)$, we assume without loss of generality that $\sup _{N\in \mathbb{N}} C^{\rm stab}_{\mkern-1muR_{\mathrm{s}},N}$ is finite. Thus the stability condition implies $\epsilon  \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$, and even $\epsilon  \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{4/3}$ if $m=5$, with constants $C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}}$ that are independent of $N$.
<!-- end paragraphesansboite-21 -->
<!-- paragraphesansboite-22: body_md -->
\label{def: errmdl errdtn} 
We fix a number $\delta $ s.t.\ $0<\delta <\min (1, \tau - \frac{1}{2} )$, for instance $\delta := \frac{1}{2} \min (1, \tau - \frac{1}{2} )$. This is possible because we have $\Theta <2\pi  \mathrel{\mbox{$\mathrel{\mbox{$\mathrel{\mbox{$\mathrel{\mbox{$\Leftarrow\hspace{-6.5pt}=$}}\hspace{-6.5pt}=$}}\hspace{-6.5pt}=$}}\hspace{-6pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\mathrel{\mbox{$=\hspace{-6.5pt}\Rightarrow$}}$}}$}}$}}  \tau > \frac{1}{2}$. Then, for~any $k\in \mathbb{N}$, $s\in \mathbb{R}$ and $R>0$, we denote
\[\errmdl[s][k] :=\displaystyle \epsilon ^{k} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-m+\delta +s} \,\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2m+1} \quad \ \text{ and } \quad \ e_{\rm dtn}^{R,s}:=\displaystyle \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau+s} \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2m+1} .\]

In addition, for any $\epsilon >0$, we introduce the notation $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}$ to denote the differential operator associated to the effective boundary condition on $\Gamma $:
\[\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
	\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}3(v) := \mu _{0} \partial _{y} v -\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } v & \text{for }  m=3\\[2pt]
	\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}5(v) := \mu _{0} \partial _{y} v -\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } v + \frac{\epsilon }{3} (\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 +\omega ^2 \rho _{1} )v & \text{for }  m=5.
\end{array}\right.\]
<!-- end paragraphesansboite-22 -->
<!-- demo-128: body_md -->
\Cref{validation construction et DA des champs} shows $u_{p,\ell } = T_{\leqslant 2} (u^0_{p,\ell } )+o_{\partial } (r^2 )$, so there exists $r_{0} >0$ s.t.\ we have on $\Gamma \cap  \{r<r_{0} \}$: $|\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} u_{p,\ell } -\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} T_{\leqslant 2} (u^0_{p,\ell } )|\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,r^{2-i-j}$. Moreover \cref{precision de l'ansatz sur uDA} yields 
\[T_{\leqslant 2} (u^0_{p,\ell } ) \,\in \sum _{d\geqslant -p+\tau} \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega )\, \subset \! \sum _{d>-p+ \frac{1}{2} +\delta } \mathcal{A}_{d} (\Omega ).\]
Thus, we have on $\Gamma \cap  \{r<r_{0} \}$: $|\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} u_{p,\ell } |\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,r^{-p+ \frac{1}{2} +\delta -i-j}$. Finally, we have $\partial _{y} ^{j} u_{p,\ell } \in H^{1} (\Omega )+\chi_0 \mathcal{A}(\Omega )$ by \cref{validation construction et DA des champs}, so $\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} u_{p,\ell }$ is also $L^2 $ on $\Gamma  \cap  \{r>r_{0} /2\}$. The bound on $\|\partial _{x} ^{i} \partial _{y} ^{j} u_{p,\ell } \|_{L^2 (\Gamma^\circ)}$ follows by integration.
<!-- end demo-128 -->
<!-- demo-129: body_md -->
By~\cref{rq: condition de stabilite et CdtnME}, the stability condition of \cref{def: condition de stabilite} implies the hypothesis ``$\epsilon \leqslant C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 1}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \,\*\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$'' of \cref{opS - opS0}. Thus \cref{opS - opS0,rq: condition de stabilite et CdtnME} show that we have
\[\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}-\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ))} \leqslant  C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 2}_{\mkern-1mu R,N} \. \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{2}} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \leqslant  \frac{C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} .\]
Hence it suffices to prove $\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),H_{\rm sc}^{j}(\Sigma^\circ))} \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} N^{j+1} /\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$. By~\cref{eq: opS positif qd eps=0 preuve expression opSref}, we have for any $v\in L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$ and $\mathbf{x} \in \Sigma^\circ$:
\[\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v)(\mathbf{x}) = \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \langle v,f _{n} \rangle  \, \partial _{r} f _{n} (\mathbf{x}) \qquad  \text{with}  \quad  f _{n} := \frac{\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} }{\|\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} }.\]
By~\cref{expression sing homog CL}, we have $\Phi^{\rm lim}_{n\pi/\Theta,0} (r,\theta )=(-1)^{n} \,\Gamma (d+1) \big( \frac{2}{k_{0}} \big)^{d} J_{d} (k_{0} r) \sin (d\theta )$ with $d:=n\tau$. This yields
\[f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} :\theta  \mapsto  \sqrt{ \frac{2}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\Theta } } \sin (d\theta ) \.\beta _{n} \qquad  \text{ and } \qquad  \partial _{r} f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} = \frac{J_{d} '(k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})}{J_{d} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})} f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} \]
for some $\beta _{n} \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\beta _{n} |=1$ (actually $\beta _{n} =(-1)^{n} (k_{0} /|k_{0} |)^{-d}$). Thus $(f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} )_{n}$ is an orthonormal family of $L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)$ and $(\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} f _{n|\Sigma^\circ} )_{n}$ is orthogonal for any $j\in \{0,1,2\}$. We deduce:
\[\big\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v) \big\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  = \sum _{n=1} ^{N} |\langle v,f _{n} \rangle |^2   \, \|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} f _{n} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  \leqslant  \|v\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  \cdot  \max _{n\in [\![1,N]\!]} \|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} f _{n} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  .\]
Moreover, by \cite{Leb72} and \cref{minoration majoration BesselJ}, we have for~any $n\in [\![1,N]\!]$:
\[\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \partial _{r} f _{n} \|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} = d^{j} \left| \frac{J_{d} '(k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})}{J_{d} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})} \right| = d^{j} \left| \frac{J_{d-1} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})-J_{d+1} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})}{2\.J_{d} (k_{0} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})} \right| \leqslant  \frac{C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} d^{j+1} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \leqslant  \frac{C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} N^{j+1} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} .\]
See \cref{estimation mcld0} for a similar reasoning. To conclude, it suffices to use
\[\big\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v) \big\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{j}(\Sigma^\circ)} ^2 = \sum\limits _{i=0} ^{j} \big\|\partial _{\theta } ^{j} \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu 0}}(v) \big\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} ^2  ,\]
see \cref{ex: sobolev pondere pour ME}.
<!-- end demo-129 -->
<!-- demo-130: body_md -->
Note that, by~definition, $\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}{u^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}}$ is a solution of \cref{eq: FV ME augmente} with homogeneous boundary conditions on $\Gamma^\circ$, $\Sigma^\circ$ and $P^\circ$. So $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}(w_{\epsilon } ) = \use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}})$, $\partial _{r} w_{\epsilon } - \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} ) = \partial _{r} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}} - \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}_{|\Sigma^\circ} )$ and likewise for $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$.
\begin{itemize}
	\item \underline{Bound on $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\feps}}3(w_{\epsilon } )$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} By~\cref{construction directe des upl}, we have on $\Gamma $:
	\begin{align}
		\mu _{0} \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}3 -\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}3 &= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P},p<3} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p,\ell } - \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P},p<3} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p-1} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p-1,\ell } \nonumber \\
		&= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P}\cap [2,3)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p,\ell } . \label{eq: erreur ME v1 preuve 1}
	\end{align}
	Let $j\in \{0,1\}$. By~\cref{estimations CL}, we have for~any $p\geqslant 2$: $\|\partial _{y} u_{p,\ell } \|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,\langle \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-p+\delta +1-j}\rangle \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-p+\delta +1-j }$ because $-p+\delta +1-j \leqslant -2+1+1\leqslant 0$. Thus we obtain:
	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
	\begin{align*}
		\big\|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}3(w_{\epsilon } )\big\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} &\leqslant  \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P}\cap [2,3)} \epsilon ^{p} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{3}} \cdot  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-p+\delta +1-j} \\
		&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon ^{2} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{3}} \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{\delta -1-j}
	\end{align*}
	because the stability condition implies $\epsilon /\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \leqslant C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}}$ by \cref{hyp: Cstab majore}.

	\item \underline{Bound on $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\feps}}5(w_{\epsilon } )$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Similarly, we have $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon } ) = \mu _{0} \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5_{|\Gamma^\circ} -\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5_{|\Gamma^\circ} + \frac{\epsilon }{3} (\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 +\omega ^2 \rho _{1} )\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5_{|\Gamma^\circ}$. By~\cref{construction directe des upl}, the second term of this is equal to:
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5 &= \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P},p<5} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p-1} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p-1,\ell } + \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P},p<5} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p-1} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \frac{\mu _{0} }{3} (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 ) \partial _{y} u_{p-3,\ell } \\
		&= \mu _{0} \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}4 + \frac{\epsilon ^2  \mu _{0} }{3} (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 ) \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}2 \qquad \text{ on }\Gamma .
	\end{align*}
	Hence we have:
	\begin{align*}
		\|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon } )\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} &= \bigg\|\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P}\cap [4,5)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p,\ell } + \frac{\epsilon  \mu _{1} }{3} (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5 -  \frac{\epsilon ^2  \mu _{0} }{3} (\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 ) \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}2 \bigg\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \\
		&\leqslant  \bigg\|\sum _{p\in \mathbb{P}\cap [4,5)} \sum _{\ell \in \mathbb{N}} \epsilon ^{p} \ln ^{\ell } \!\epsilon \, \mu _{0} \partial _{y} u_{p,\ell } \bigg\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} + \frac{\epsilon  \mu _{1} }{3} \big\|(\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5-\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}3)\big\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \\
		& \qquad  + \frac{\epsilon ^2 }{3} \Big\|(\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )\underbrace{\left(\frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}3-\mu _{0} \partial _{y} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}2\right)}_{\textstyle =0 \text{ by \cref{eq: erreur ME v1 preuve 1}} } \Big\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)}
	\end{align*}
	The first term can be bounded in the same way as for $\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}3(w_{\epsilon } )$. Moreover, by \cref{estimations CL} we have for~any $p\geqslant 3$: $\|\partial _{x} ^2  u_{p,\ell } \|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-p+\delta -j}$ because $-p+\delta -j\leqslant -3+1\leqslant 0$. This allows us to bound the second term: 
	\[\frac{\epsilon  \mu _{1} }{3} \.\big\|(\partial _{x} ^2 +k_{1} ^2 )(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5-\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}3)\big\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  \sum _{p\in \mathbb{P}\cap [3,5)} \epsilon ^{p+1} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{5}} \cdot  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},p} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-p+\delta -j} .\]
	It is easy to deduce similarly $\|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon } )\|_{H^{j} (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon ^{4} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{5}} \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{\delta -3-j}$.

	\item \underline{Bound on $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\feps}}(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let $h:=\partial _{r} w_{\epsilon } - \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )$ and
	\[\tilde{u} := \sum _{n=1} ^{N} \sigma _{n\tau} (u^{\rm f{}f\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 0}_{m,\epsilon}) \cdot \use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{n} \,\in \,\operatorname{Span}(\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{1} ,\dots ,\use@eps{\Psi^{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}_{N} ).\]
	By~construction of $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}$ (see \cref{sec: construction de opS et opP}) we have $\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}( \tilde{u}_{|\Sigma^\circ} )=\partial _{r} \tilde{u}_{|\Sigma^\circ}$. Thus
	\[h = \partial _{r} \use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}_{|\Sigma^\circ} -\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}_{|\Sigma^\circ} ) = \partial _{r} (\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}- \tilde{u})_{|\Sigma^\circ} -\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}_{|\Sigma^\circ} - \tilde{u}_{|\Sigma^\circ} ) \]
	which implies
	\[\|h\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant  \|\partial _{r} (\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}- \tilde{u})\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}  + \|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ))} \|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}- \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} .\]
	Besides, thanks to \cref{hyp: Cstab majore}, the stability condition implies $\epsilon \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} ^{\star} \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$ for some constant $C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} ^{\star}$. Applying \cref{decompo modale SE 2} with $M:=C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} ^{\star}$ and \cref{norme opS}, we obtain
	\[\|h\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \, \frac{N}{\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}} \left[ \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau+ \frac{1}{2} }  + \frac{\epsilon ^{m} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{m-\tau}} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \right] \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2m+1} .\]
	Finally, we bound the factor $1/\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{m-\tau}$ by $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-m+\delta + \frac{1}{2} }$.

	\item \underline{Bound on $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\feps}}5(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )$:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} By~\cref{rq: condition de stabilite et CdtnME}, the assumptions of \cref{opS - opS0} are fulfilled, so we have $\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\mathbb{C})} \leqslant  C^{\rm DtN\mkern-0.5mu,\mkern0.5mu 2}_{\mkern-1mu R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\epsilon \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-2} \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}$. Using again \cref{rq: condition de stabilite et CdtnME}, this implies $\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\mathbb{C})} \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} /\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$, where this bound is independent of $N$. Moreover, we have $\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5( \tilde{u}_{|\Sigma^\circ} )=\partial _{x} \tilde{u}(P^\circ)$, so \cref{decompo modale SE 2} gives
	\begin{align*}
		\big|\partial _{x} w_{\epsilon } (P^\circ) - \use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )\big| &= \frac{\mu _{1} }{3} \Big| \partial _{x} (\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5- \tilde{u})(P^\circ) -\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5_{|\Sigma^\circ} - \tilde{u}_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\Big| \\
		&\leqslant  C\,| \partial _{x} (\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5- \tilde{u})(P^\circ)| + C \.\|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),\mathbb{C})} \,\|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}5- \tilde{u}\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \\
		&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \, \frac{1}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \left[ \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau+ \frac{1}{2} }  + \frac{\epsilon ^{m} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{m-\tau}} \.\langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \right] \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2\cdot 5+1}
	\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end demo-130 -->
<!-- demo-131: body_md -->
It suffices to combine \cref{caractere bien pose des ME augmentes,erreur consistence ME}. For $w$, we have if $m=3$
\[\|w3\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C^{\rm stab}_{\rm s} \,\|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}3(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}}3)\|_{L^2 (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\errmdl[2][m-1] ,\]
and likewise for $m=5$. As~for $w$, we have when $m=3$:
\[\|w3\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C^{\rm stab}_{\rm s} \.\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \.\big\|\partial _{r} w_{\epsilon } - \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}3(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )\big\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \,N \big( \errmdl[1/2] + e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/2} \big).\]
Similarly, when $m=5$, we have
\begin{multline*}
	\|w5\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \.\lvertw5\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  C^{\rm stab}_{\rm s} \.\Big( \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \.\big\|\partial _{r} w_{\epsilon } - \use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )\big\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	{}+\sqrt{\epsilon } \.\big|\partial _{x} w_{\epsilon } (P^\circ) - \use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}5(w_{\epsilon |\Sigma^\circ} )\big| \Big)
\end{multline*}
Then we use that the stability condition implies $\epsilon \leqslant C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{4/3}$ (see \cref{hyp: Cstab majore}), so $\sqrt{\epsilon } \leqslant C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{2/3}$:
\begin{align*}
	\|w5\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \.\lvertw5\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} &\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \,N \big( \errmdl[1/2] + e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/2} \big) + C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \.\big( \errmdl[1/6] + e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/6} \big)\\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \,N \big(\errmdl[1/6] + e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/6} \big)
\end{align*}
<!-- end demo-131 -->

\def\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon{\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon} 
\def\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}} 
\def\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}} 
For~any $u,v\in H^{1} (\Omega )$ let us define
\[a(u,v) := \int _{\Omega^\circ} (\mu _{0} \nabla  u \cdot  \nabla  \bar{v}- \omega ^2  \rho _{0} \.u \bar{v}) \qquad  \text{ and } \qquad  \tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon(u,v) := \int _{\Sigma^\circ} \mu _{0} \,\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(u_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\, \bar{v}.\]
Similarly to \cref{coercivite partie hors DtN des ME}, $a$ satisfies the uniform coercivity property: $\forall u\in H^{1} (\Omega ),\; \Im( \overline{\omega }) \*\,\Im( \overline{\omega }\,a(u,u))\geqslant  C\.\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2 $. In a very similar way to \cref{caractere bien pose des ME augmentes}, one can prove that there exists $C^{\mathrm{dir}} _{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} >0$ s.t., under the assumptions $\epsilon \leqslant  C^{\mathrm{dir}} _{R_{\mathrm{s}},N} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{-3}$ and $R\leqslant R_{\mathrm{s}}$, $a+\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon$ is uniformly coercive and uniformly continuous:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
\[\forall u\in H^{1} (\Omega ), \quad  C\.\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2  \leqslant  \big|a(u,u)+\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon(u,u)\big| \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \. \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}^2 .\]
Let us show that there exists $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}} \in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3$ s.t.\ $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}_{|\Gamma^\circ} =g_{\rm s}$ and $\|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1/2} \.\|g_{\rm s}\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)}$. We recall that $\use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3:=\{u\in H^{1} (\Omega^\circ) \mid u_{|\Sigma_\Omega^\circ} =0\}$.
\begin{sousdemo}
	Let $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}} \in H^{1} (\Omega  \setminus \overline{B}(0,1))$ be s.t.\ $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}_{|\Gamma } =g_{\rm s}(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\vcenter{\hbox{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}} \.)$, $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}_{|\Sigma_\Omega} =0$ and $\|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}\|_{H^{1}} \leqslant  C\.\|g_{\rm s}(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\vcenter{\hbox{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}} \.)\|_{H^{1/2} }$. Let $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}:x\mapsto \@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}(x/\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})$. We have $\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}} \in \use@m{H_{\@nextchar}}3$ and, by~definition of $H_{\rm sc}^{1}$ (see \cref{def: sobolev pondere pour ME}),
	\[\|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} = \left(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2  \.\|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} ^2  +\|\nabla \@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} ^2 \right)^{ \frac{1}{2} } \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm sc}}{u_{\rm sc}}\|_{H^{1}} \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1/2} \.\|g_{\rm s}\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)} .\vspace{-2ex}\]
\end{sousdemo}
Let $H:=\{u\in H^{1} (\Omega^\circ) \mid u_{|\Sigma_\Omega^\circ\cup \Gamma^\circ} =0\}$. $u$ is a solution of \cref{eq: ME avec Dirichlet sur Gamma} iff $u_{0} :=u-\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}$ satisfies $u_{0} \in H$ and
\[\forall v\in H,\qquad  a(u_{0} ,v)+\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon(u_{0} ,v) = -a(\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}},v)-\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon(\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}},v).\]
By~uniform coercivity and continity of $a+\tilde{b}^{(m)}_\epsilon$ and using Lax-Milgram's theorem, this problem has a unique solution and it satisfies $\|u_{0} \|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C\.\|\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru_{\rm lift}}{u_{\rm lift}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1/2} \.\|g_{\rm s}\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)}$.

\phantomsection\label{preuve: cvg des ME} 
By~\cref{hyp: Cstab majore}, the stability condition implies $\epsilon \leqslant C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \.\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$, so we can apply \cref{regularite elliptique pour ME 2} with $M:=C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}}$. By~construction of $w$ in \cref{eq: def emeg}, this gives 
\begin{align*}
	\|w\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)} &\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon \. \bigg( \|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}})\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1}(\Gamma^\circ)} + \|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} +  \frac{\|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{3/2}} \\
	&\quad {}+ \delta _{m,5} \.\sqrt{ \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} } \.\lvertw\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \bigg) \,+\, C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{3/2} \, \big|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )(P^\circ)\big| \\[2pt]
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon \. \bigg( \|\use@m{\mathbf{D}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\epsilon}}(\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}})\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1}(\Gamma^\circ)} + \|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	&\quad {}+ \frac{\|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \delta _{m,5} \.\sqrt{\epsilon } \.\lvertw\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)}}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{3/2}} \bigg) \,+\, C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{3/2} \, \big|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\big| 
	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
	                                                                        
\end{align*}
Here $\delta _{m,5}$ indicates that the associated term should be ignored when $m=3$. By~\cref{erreur consistence ME,erreur ME v1}, this yields\vspace{-0.5ex}
\begin{align*}
	\|w\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)} &\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon \. \left( C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\errmdl[2][m-1] + \big\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\big\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} + C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \errmdl[1/2][m-1] \right) \\
	&\quad {}+ C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{3/2} \, \big|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\big| .
\end{align*}
Besides, we have
\begin{alignjustif}[\quad]
	\big\|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\big\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} &\leqslant  \|\use@m{\mathbf{S}^{(\@nextchar)}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}\|_{\mathcal{L}(L^2 (\Sigma^\circ),H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ))} \,\|w\|_{L^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}}} \frac{N^{3} }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \cdot  \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \.\|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} & \text{by \cref{opS - opS0,eq: norme L2 SME vs H1 OME}} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \.\errmdl[3/2][m-1] N^{3} & \text{by \cref{erreur ME v1}} . 
\end{alignjustif}
Similarly,
\[\big|\use@m{\mathbf{P}^{(\@nextchar)}_{\!N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}}(w_{|\Sigma^\circ} )\big| \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon  \left( \frac{N}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \right)^{5/2} \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3}  \cdot \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\errmdl[2][m-1] \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,e_{\rm model}^{#2,\,}\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,N^{5/2} .\]
Hence
\begin{align*}
	\|w\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)} &\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\epsilon  \left( \errmdl[2][m-1] + \errmdl[3/2][m-1] N^{3} + \errmdl[1/2][m-1] \right) + C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \,\errmdl[3/2] \,N^{5/2} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} \errmdl[1/2] \,\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,N^{3} .
\end{align*}
Then \cref{ME avec Dirichlet sur Gamma} implies $\|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} e_{\rm model}^{#2,\,}\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,N^2 $. Next, using one more time \cref{erreur ME v1}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
	\|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} &\leqslant  \|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \|w\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}}} e_{\rm model}^{#2,\,}\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,N^{3} + C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \,N \left( \errmdl[1/6] + e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/6} \right) \\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left( e_{\rm model}^{#2,\,}\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{3} \,N^{3} + C_{R} \,e_{\rm dtn}^{R,1/6} N \right)
\end{align*}
By~\cref{def: errmdl errdtn}, this means that we have
\begin{align}
	\|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} &\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left[ \left( \frac{\epsilon \mathstrut}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \right)^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \cdot  \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{\delta } \.\langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2m+4} \cdot  N^{3} + \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau+ \frac{1}{6} } \langle \ln \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\rangle^{2m+1} \cdot  N \right] \nonumber\\
	&\leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left[ \bigg( \frac{\epsilon \mathstrut}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \bigg)^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \,N^{3} + \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau} \!N \right] \label{eq: cvg des ME preuve}
\end{align}
Let $R' :=(R+R_{\mathrm{s}})/2 \in (R,R_{\mathrm{s}})$. Applying \cref{eq: cvg des ME preuve} to $R'$ instead of $R$, and using the following bound
\[\left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R'} \right)^{N\tau} \!N = \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau} \left( \frac{R}{R'} \right)^{N\tau} \!N \leqslant  C_{R_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau} ,\]
we can eliminate $N$ from the right term of \cref{eq: cvg des ME preuve}, which gives:
\[\|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  C_{f_{\mathrm{s}},R} \left[ \bigg( \frac{\epsilon \mathstrut}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \bigg)^{m} \langle \ln \epsilon \rangle^{\ell _{m}} \,N^{3} + \left( \frac{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}{R} \right)^{N\tau} \right] .\]
Finally, by \cref{DA de SE avec CL et delta variable}, $\|u_{\epsilon } -\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}$ is controlled by the same bound. We conclude by writing $\|u_{\epsilon } -\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}{u^{(\@nextchar)}_\epsilon}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} \leqslant  \|u_{\epsilon } -\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscru^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}{u^{\rm f{}f}_{\@nextchar,\epsilon}}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} +\|\use@m{\@ifnextchar_{\open@subscrw_\epsilon}{w_\epsilon}}\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}$.

\phantomsection\label{preuve: regularite elliptique pour ME} 
\defR{R}                                  
\defR'{R'}                                  
\defI_\Theta{J}                                  
\defw{\tilde u} 
\def\tilde f{\tilde f} 
\def\tilde g{\tilde g} 
\def\mathscr P{\mathscr P}           
\def\operatorname{Lip}{\operatorname{Lip}} 
The proof has two steps. First we prove that $u$ is $H^2 $ in $R':=I_\Theta\times (0, \frac{\eta }{2} )$ and we bound $\|u\|_{H^2 (R')}$ using finite differences. Then we rewrite the boundary condition as $\nu _{1} u = \epsilon \,(g-\partial _{n} u+\dots )$ to deduce $\|u\|_{H^{1/2} (I_\Theta_{0} )} =O(\epsilon )$. The first step is the longest part.\medskip

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} We focus on the second point (with Ventcel's condition), as the first one is simpler. We will explain in the end what should be modified for Robin's condition. Let $\mathscr P:=\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}_+^*$. Let $\chi \in \mathcal{C}^2 (\overline{\mathscr P})$ be s.t.\ $\chi =1$ in $R'$, $\chi =0$ outside $R$, and $\chi $ and its derivatives are bounded. We also assume that $\partial _{y} \chi _{|\partial \mathscr P} =0$ (such a function $\chi $ is not difficult to construct). Let $w :\mathscr P\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be the extension of $\chi u$ by 0 outside $R$. We clearly have $w \in H^{1} (\mathscr P)$ and $w$ satisfies
\[\left\{\begin{array}{r@{}l@{}ll}
	\operatorname{div}(A \nabla w) &{}= \chi  f+ 2A \nabla  \chi \cdot \nabla  u+\operatorname{div}(A \nabla  \chi )\,u &{} =:\tilde f &\text{ in }\mathscr P \\[.5ex]
	\partial _{n} w + \frac{\nu _{1} }{\epsilon } w - \epsilon \,\nu _{2} \partial _{x} ^2 w &{}=\chi  g-\cancel{\partial _{y} \chi }\,u +2\epsilon  \nu _{2} \,\partial _{x} \chi  \,\partial _{x} u +\epsilon  \nu _{2} \partial _{x} ^2 \chi  \,u &{} = \chi g+\epsilon \tilde g &\text{ on }\partial \mathscr P=\mathbb{R}\times \{0\}
\end{array}\right.\]
with $\tilde f \in L^2 (\mathscr P)$, $\chi g \in H^{1} (\partial \mathscr P)$ and $\tilde g:=2\nu _{2} \partial _{x} \chi  \,\partial _{x} u +\nu _{2} \partial _{x} ^2 \chi  \,u \in L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)$. Since $A$ is the identity matrix on $I_{0}$, the associated variational formulation is:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve FV}}
	\int _{\mathscr P} A \nabla  w\cdot \nabla  \bar{v}+ \int _{\partial \mathscr P} \left(\frac{\nu _{1} }{\epsilon } \,w \bar{v}+\epsilon  \,\nu _{2} \,\partial _{x} w \,\partial _{x} \bar{v}\right) = -\int _{\mathscr P} \tilde f \bar{v}+\int _{\partial \mathscr P} (\chi g+\epsilon \tilde g) \bar{v}.
\end{equation}
Let us denote $D_{h} f :(x,y)\mapsto \frac{f (x+h,y)-f (x,y)}{h}$ for~any $h\in \mathbb{R}^*$ and $f :\mathscr P\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ (and similarly for $f :\partial \mathscr P\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$). Taking $v:=D_{-h} D_{h} w$ in \cref{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve FV} and doing discrete integrations by parts, we obtain:
\begin{multline*}
	\int _{\mathscr P} D_{h} (A\nabla  w)\cdot D_{h} \nabla  \barw + \int _{\partial \mathscr P} \left( \frac{\nu _{1} }{\epsilon } |D_{h} w|^2  +\epsilon  \nu _{2} |D_{h} \partial _{x} w|^2  \right) \\
	= \int _{\mathscr P} \tilde f \cdot D_{-h} D_{h} \barw -\int _{\partial \mathscr P} D_{h} (\chi g) \cdot  D_{h} \barw -\int _{\partial \mathscr P} \epsilon \tilde g \cdot D_{-h} D_{h} \barw .
\end{multline*}
Now we have $D_{h} (A f )=D_{h} A \cdot f +A \cdot D_{h} f $ with $f :=\nabla w$. Passing the term $D_{h} A \cdot f $ to the right-hand side and using $\|D_{h} A\|_{L^{\infty }} \leqslant \operatorname{Lip}(A)$, we get:
\begin{multline*}
	\int _{\mathscr P} A D_{h} \nabla  w \cdot  D_{h} \nabla  \barw + \int _{\partial \mathscr P} \left( \frac{\nu _{1} }{\epsilon } |D_{h} w |^2  +\epsilon  \nu _{2} |D_{h} \partial _{x} w|^2  \right) \\
	\leqslant  \|\tilde f\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \|D_{-h} D_{h} w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} +\|D_{h} (\chi g)\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \|D_{h} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \\
	+\epsilon  \.\|\tilde g\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \|D_{-h} D_{h} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} + \operatorname{Lip}(A) \|\nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \|D_{h} \nabla  w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} .
\end{multline*}
Then we use the ellipticity assumption in the left-hand side, and we bound some $\|D_{\pm h} \cdot \|_{L^2 }$ by $\|\partial _{x} \cdot \|_{L^2 }$ in the right-hand side. This gives:
                                    
\begin{multline*}
	S:=\|D_{h} \nabla  w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  + \frac{1}{\epsilon } \|D_{h} w \|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} ^2  +\epsilon  \.\|D_{h} \partial _{x} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} ^2  \\
	\begin{array}{l@{}l@{}}
		\leqslant  C_{A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} } \Big( & \|\tilde f\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \|D_{h} \nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} +\|\partial _{x} (\chi g)\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \|D_{h} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \\[2\jot]
		& {} + \epsilon  \.\|\tilde g\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} \|D_{h} \partial _{x} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)}
		+ \|\nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \|D_{h} \nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \Big)\!\! \\[2\jot]
		\underset{\mathclap{\rm C.S.}}\leqslant \displaystyle C_{A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} } \big(& \|\tilde f\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  +\epsilon  \.\|\partial _{x} (\chi g)\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} + \epsilon  \.\|\tilde g\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} ^2 + \|\nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  \big)^{1/2} \cdot S^{1/2} .
	\end{array}
\end{multline*}
Now, we simplify the factor $S^{1/2}$ on both sides, we take the limit $h\rightarrow 0$, and we use the estimates $\|\tilde f\|_{L^2 } \leqslant C_{\chi ,A} (\|f\|_{L^2 } +\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)})$, $\|\partial _{x} (\chi g)\|_{L^2 } \leqslant C_{\chi } \|g\|_{H^{1}}$, $\|\tilde g\|_{L^2 } \leqslant C_{\chi ,\nu _{2}} (\snh{u}(I_{0} )+\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)})$ and $\|\nabla  w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} \leqslant C_{\chi } \|u\|_{H^{1} (R)}$. This gives:
\begin{align*}
	\|\partial _{x} \nabla  w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  &\leqslant  \limsup\limits _{h\rightarrow 0} \|D_{h} \nabla  w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  \\
	&\leqslant  C_{A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} } \big(\|\tilde f\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  +\epsilon \.\|\partial _{x} (\chi g)\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} ^2 +\epsilon \.\|\tilde g\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)} ^2  + \|\nabla w\|_{L^2 (\mathscr P)} ^2  \big) \\[\jot]
	&\leqslant  C_{I,J,\eta ,A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} ,\epsilon _{0} } \big(\|f\|_{L^2 (R)} ^2 + \epsilon \.\|g\|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )} ^2   +\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)} ^2  + \epsilon \.\snh{u}(I_{0} )^2  \big).
\end{align*}
Since $w_{|R'} =u_{|R'}$ and $\partial _{y} ^2 u = f-\partial _{x} ^2 u$ in $R'$, we deduce in particular $u_{|R'}\in H^2 $ and
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve H2 recJ}}
	\|u\|_{H^2 (R')} \leqslant  C_{I,I_\Theta,\eta ,A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} ,\epsilon _{0} } \big(\|f\|_{L^2 (R)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \,\|g\|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )}  +\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \,\snh{u}(I_{0} ) \big).
\end{equation}
Similarly, in the Robin case (i.e.\ when $\partial _{n} u + \frac{\nu _{1} }{\epsilon } u=g$ on $I_{0}$), one can prove $\|u\|_{H^2 (R')} \leqslant  C_{I,I_\Theta,\eta ,A,\nu _{1} } \*\big(\|f\|_{L^2 (R)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \.\|g\|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )} +\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)} \big)$. It suffices to replace $\nu _{2}$ and $\tilde g$ by 0 and to ignore the terms that involve $\|D_{h} \partial _{x} w\|_{L^2 (\partial \mathscr P)}$.\medskip\smallskip

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} For the Robin case, the estimate on $\|u\|_{H^{1/2} (I_\Theta_{0} )}$ is a direct consequence of $u_{|I_\Theta_{0}} = \frac{\epsilon }{\nu _{1}} (g-\partial _{n} u)$, the inequality $\|\partial _{n} u\|_{H^{1/2} (I_\Theta_{0} )} \leqslant  C_{I_\Theta,\eta } \|u\|_{H^2 (R')}$ and step 1. The Ventcel case is less obvious because we have $u_{|I_\Theta_{0}} = \frac{\epsilon }{\nu _{1}} (g-\partial _{n} u +\nu _{2} \partial _{x} ^2 u)$ with no control over $\|\partial _{x} ^2 u\|_{H^{1/2} (I_\Theta_{0} )}$ for now. To conclude in this case, we will do one more step of elliptic regularity on $\partial \mathscr P$.\\
\defw{w} 
Let $K$ be an open interval of $\mathbb{R}$ s.t.\ $\overline{J}\subset K$ and $\overline{K}\subset I$. We denote $K_{0} :=K\times \{0\}$. Let $\chi  \in  \mathcal{C}^2 (\partial \mathscr P)$ be a new truncation function s.t.\ $\chi _{|I_\Theta_{0}} =1$ and $\chi _{|\mathbb{R} \setminus K_{0} }=0$. Let $w:=\chi  u_{|K_{0}}$ extended by 0 outside $K_{0}$. The boundary condition of $u$ on $I_{0}$ implies:
\begin{equation}{\label{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve pb sur ddpl}}
	-\epsilon ^2 \nu _{2} \partial _{x} ^2 w + \nu _{1} w = \epsilon  \chi  g-\epsilon  \chi  \partial _{n} u -\epsilon ^2 \nu _{2} (2 \partial _{x} \chi  \,\partial _{x} u +\partial _{x} ^2 \chi  \,u ) =: h \quad \text{ on }\partial \mathscr P.
\end{equation}
\Cref{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve H2 recJ} of step 1 applied to $K$ instead of $J$ implies
\begin{align*}
	\|h\|_{H^{1/2} (\partial \mathscr P)} &\leqslant  C_{\chi ,\nu _{2}} \,\epsilon \, \big(\|g\|_{H^{1/2} (I_{0} )} + \|\partial _{n} u\|_{H^{1/2} (K_{0} )} + \epsilon \.\|u\|_{H^{3/2} (K_{0} )} \big)\\
	&\leqslant  C_{I_\Theta,K,\eta ,\nu _{2} ,\epsilon _{0} } \,\epsilon \, \big(\|g\|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )} + \|u\|_{H^2 (K\times (0,\eta /2))} \big)\\
	&\leqslant  C_{I,I_\Theta,\eta ,A,\nu _{1} ,\nu _{2} ,\epsilon _{0} } \,\epsilon \, \big(\|f\|_{L^2 (R)} + \|g\|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )}  +\|u\|_{H^{1} (R)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \,\snh{u}(I_{0} ) \big).
\end{align*}
Applying the one-dimensional Fourier transform on $\partial \mathscr P$ to \cref{eq: regularite elliptique pour ME preuve pb sur ddpl} gives $(\epsilon ^2 \nu _{2} \xi ^2 +\nu _{1} )\hatw= \hat{h}$, so $\nu _{1} |\hatw|\leqslant | \hat{h}|$. Therefore\vspace{-2pt}
\[\smash{\|u\|_{H^{1/2} (I_\Theta_{0} )} \leqslant  \|w\|_{H^{1/2} (\partial \mathscr P)} = \big\| (1+\xi ^2 )\hatw \big\|_{L^2 (\mathbb{R})} \leqslant  \frac{1}{\nu _{1}} \.\big\| (1+\xi ^2 )\hat h \big\|_{L^2 (\mathbb{R})} = \frac{1}{\nu _{1}} \.\|h\|_{H^{1/2} (\partial \mathscr P)} .}\]
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end demo-137 -->

\phantomsection\label{preuve: diffeo ME} 
\def\phi{\phi} 
\defE{E} 
\def(-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\infty){(-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\infty)} 
\defI_\Theta{I_\Theta} 
\def(-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\infty)\timesI_\Theta{(-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\infty)\timesI_\Theta} 
\def\Omega'{\Omega'} 
\def\Gamma'{\Gamma'} 
\def\Sigma'{\Sigma'} 
\def\psi_2{\psi_2} 
                                                                                                             
Let $(r,\theta )$ denote the polar coordinates with $\theta  \in (-\pi , \pi )$ and let $\rho :=r-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$. We define $I_\Theta:=(-\pi ,\pi )\cap (\Theta -2\pi ,\Theta )$, $E:=\{(x,y)\in \mathbb{R}^2  \setminus (\mathbb{R}_-\times \{0\}) \mid \theta (x,y)\in I_\Theta\}$ and
\[\phi :\left( \begin{array}{ccc}
	E & \rightarrow  & (-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\infty)\timesI_\Theta\\[2pt]
	(x,y) & \mapsto  & (\rho ,\theta )
\end{array} \right) .\]
We will build $f $ as $\psi \circ \phi$ with $\psi :\mathbb{R}^2  \rightarrow  \mathbb{R}^2 $ ($V_{1}$ and $V_{2}$ will be defined later). Let $\Omega':=(\mathbb{R}_+^*)^2 $, $\Gamma':=\mathbb{R}_+^*\times \{0\}$ and $\Sigma':=\{0\}\times \mathbb{R}_+^*$. It is clear that $\phi$ satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\phi$ is a $\mathcal{C}^{\infty }$-diffeomorphism,
	                                                                                                                                            
	\item $\phi(P^\circ)=0$, $\phi(\Omega^\circ \cap E)=\Omega' \cap \phi(E)$, $\phi(\Gamma^\circ \cap E)=\Gamma' \cap \phi(E)$, $\phi(\Sigma^\circ \cap E)=\Sigma' \cap \phi(E)$ (thanks to the definition of $I_\Theta$)
	\item $\forall (x,y) \in \Gamma' \cap E, \; \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}\phi(x,y) = \mathrm{Diag} (1,1/x)$,
	\item $\forall (x,y) \in \Sigma' \cap E, \; \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}\phi(x,y) = \mathrm{Diag} (1,1/\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})\circ R_{-\theta }$.
\end{itemize}
Hence, it suffices that $\psi $ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
	\item $\psi (0) = 0$, $\psi (\Omega') = \Omega'$, $\psi (\Gamma') = \Gamma'$, $\psi (\Sigma') = \Sigma'$,
	\item $\psi $ is differentiable and $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} \psi $ is Lipschitz,
	\item $\forall (\rho ,\theta ) \in \Gamma', \; \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} \psi (\rho ,\theta ) = \mathrm{Diag} (1,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+\rho )$,
	\item $\forall (\rho ,\theta ) \in \Sigma', \; \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} \psi (\rho ,\theta ) = \mathrm{Diag} (1,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})$,
	\item there exist two neighborhoods $V',V_{2}$ of 0 in $\mathbb{R}^2 $ s.t.\ $\psi $ is a $\mathcal{C}^{1}$-diffeomorphism from $V'$ to $V_{2}$, and $V'\subset \phi(E)$ (then it suffices to take $V_{1} :=\phi^{-1} (V')$).
\end{enumerate}
Let $\chi \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty } (\mathbb{R},[0,1])$ be equal to 0 in a vicinity of $-\infty $, and to 1 in a vicinity of $+\infty $. For~any $(\rho ,\theta )\in \mathbb{R}^2 $, we define:\vspace{-0.5ex}
\[\psi (\rho ,\theta ) := (\rho ,\psi_2(\rho ,\theta )) \qquad  \text{with}  \qquad  \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) := \left\{\begin{array}{@{\;}ll@{}}
	\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \theta  & \text{if } \rho \leqslant 0\\
	(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+\rho \,\chi (\ln \rho -\ln \theta ))\,\theta  & \text{if } \rho >0 \text{ and } \theta >0\\
	(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+\rho ) \theta  & \text{if } \rho >0 \text{ and } \theta =0\\
	-\psi_2(\rho ,-\theta ) & \text{if } \rho >0 \text{ and } \theta <0.
\end{array}\right.\]
It is clear that (i) is satisfied. Moreover, $\psi $ is differentiable in $\mathbb{R}^2  \setminus \{0\}$ because:
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\psi_2$ is $\mathcal{C}^{\infty }$ in $\mathbb{R}_+^*\times \mathbb{R}^* = \Omega' \cup  (\mathbb{R}_+^*\times \mathbb{R}_-^*)$,
	\item $\psi_2(\rho ,\theta )$ is equal to $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \theta $ in an open subset of $\Omega'$ that contains $(\mathbb{R}_-\times \mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$,
	\item $\psi_2(\rho ,\theta )$ is equal to $(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} +\rho )\theta $ in an open subset of  $\Omega'$ that contains $\Gamma'$,
	\item and these three open sets cover $\mathbb{R}^2  \setminus \{0\}$.
\end{itemize}
Let us show that $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} \psi $ is Lipschitz on $\mathbb{R}^2  \setminus \{0\}$.
\begin{sousdemo}
	Let us show that $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon}\psi_2$ is Lipschitz in $\Omega'$, because the rest is easy.
	Let $(\rho ,\theta )\in \Omega'$. We have\vspace{-2pt}
	\[\!\Bigg\{ \begin{array}{@{\;}r@{\,=\,}l}
		\partial _{\rho } \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) & \theta  \cdot  (\chi +\chi ')(\ln \rho -\ln \theta ) \\[3pt]
		\partial _{\theta } \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) & \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} + \rho  \cdot  (\chi -\chi ')(\ln \rho -\ln \theta )
	\end{array} 
	\quad \  \mathrm{so} \quad \ 
	\left\{\begin{array}{@{\,}r@{\,=\,}l}
		\partial _{\rho } ^2  \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) & \frac{\theta }{\rho } \cdot  (\chi '+\chi '')(\ln \rho -\ln \theta ) \\[3pt]
		\partial _{\rho } \partial _{\theta } \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) & (\chi -\chi '')(\ln \rho -\ln \theta ) \\[4pt]
		\partial _{\theta } ^2 \psi_2(\rho ,\theta ) & \frac{\rho }{\theta } \cdot  (\chi ''-\chi ')(\ln \rho -\ln \theta ).
	\end{array} \right.\]
	Let $M>0$ be s.t.\ $\operatorname{supp}(\chi ')\subset [-M,M]$. We deduce $|\partial _{\rho } ^2  \psi_2(\rho ,\theta )| \leqslant  e^{M} \|\chi '+\chi ''\|_{L^{\infty }}$, $|\partial _{\rho } \partial _{\theta } \psi_2(\rho ,\theta )| \leqslant \|\chi -\chi ''\|_{L^{\infty }}$ and $|\partial _{\theta } ^2  \psi_2(\rho ,\theta )| \leqslant  e^{M} \|\chi ''-\chi '\|_{L^{\infty }}$. Thus $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} ^2 f $ is bounded on $\Omega'$, so $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f $ is Lipschitz.
\end{sousdemo}
In~particular $\lim _{\mathbf{x}\rightarrow 0} \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f $ exists. This yields that $\psi $ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^2 $ and proves (ii). Moreover (iii) and (iv) are easy to verify. Finally, (v) is a direct consequence of the inverse function theorem, as $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f (0)=\mathrm{Diag} (1,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ})$ is invertible.
<!-- end demo-138 -->

\phantomsection\label{preuve: regularite elliptique pour ME 2} 
We only prove the second point, as the first one is simpler. First, we assume that $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}=1$, then we will extend the result to any $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$ by a scaling method.\medskip

\underline{Step 1:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let us assume that $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}=1$, $0<\epsilon \leqslant M$ and 
\begingroup\let\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}=1 
\[\left\{\begin{array}{r@{}ll}
	\Delta u &{}= f &\text{ in }\Omega^\circ\\
	\mu _{0} \partial _{n} u + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } u - \epsilon \,(\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 +\omega ^2 \rho _{1} )u &{}=g &\text{ on }\Gamma^\circ\\
	\partial _{r} u &{}= h &\text{ on }\Sigma^\circ \text{ and } \text{at }  P^\circ
\end{array}\right.\]
for some $f\in L^2 (\Omega^\circ)$. Let $f :V_{1} \rightarrow V_{2}$ be the diffeomorphism given by \cref{diffeo ME}. Let $a>0$ be s.t.\ $[\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+a)\cap \{0\} \subset V_{1}$. We define $I:=(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{a}{5} ,\infty )$, $J:=(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{2a}{5} ,\infty )$ and we take $\eta >0$ s.t.\ $I\times (0,\eta )\subset \Omega^\circ$. Let $\tilde{g} := g-\epsilon \,\omega ^2 \rho _{1} u_{|\Gamma^\circ}$. We apply \cref{regularite elliptique pour ME} on $u$ with these values of $I,J,\eta , \tilde{g}$, with $A$ the identity matrix, and with $\nu _{1} :=\mu _{1}$ and $\nu _{2} := \mu _{1} /3$. This gives
\begin{align*}
	\smash{\|u\|_{H^{1/2} ((\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{2a}{5} ,\infty )\times \{0\})} } &\leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon \,\big(\|f\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} + \| \tilde{g} \|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)} +\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} +\sqrt{\epsilon } \,\lvertu\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \big) \\
	&\leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon \,\big( \|f\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} + \|\textcolor{red!93!black}{g}\|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)} +\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} + \sqrt{\epsilon } \, \lvertu\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \big).
\end{align*}
It remains to treat the vicinity of $P^\circ$. Let $v:\Omega^\circ\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be defined in polar coordinates by $v(r,\theta ):= r\cdot h(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\theta )$. The function $u_{1} :=u+v$ satisfies
\[\left\{\begin{array}{@{\,}r@{}l@{\;}l}
	\Delta u_{1} &{}= f_{1} := f+\Delta v&\text{ in }\Omega^\circ\\
	\mu _{0} \partial _{n} u_{1} + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } u_{1} - \epsilon \.\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 u_{1} &{}=g_{1} := \tilde{g} + \mu _{0} \partial _{\theta } h(P^\circ) + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } \.r \.h(P^\circ) &\text{ on }\Gamma^\circ\\
	\partial _{r} u_{1} &{}= 0 &\text{ on }\Sigma^\circ \text{ and } \text{at }  P^\circ
\end{array}\right.\]
Now let $u_{2} = u_{1} \circ f ^{-1}$, $g_{2} = g_{1} \circ f ^{-1}$, $f_{2} =(\det(\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f )^{-1} f_{1} )\circ f ^{-1}$ and $A = [\det(\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f )^{-1} \cdot \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f \cdot \tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f ^{\mathsf{T}} ]\circ f ^{-1}$, where $f ^{-1} :V_{2} \rightarrow V_{1}$ is the inverse function of $f $ and $\det(\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f )^{-1} :x\mapsto  1/\det(\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f (x))$. The properties of $f $ (see \cref{diffeo ME}) imply:
\begin{equation}{\label{regularite elliptique pour ME 2 preuve u2}}
\left\{\begin{array}{@{\,}r@{}l@{\;}l}
	\operatorname{div}(A \nabla  u_{2} ) &{}= f_{2} &\text{ in }(\mathbb{R}_+^*)^2  \cap V_{2} \\[1pt]
	\mu _{0} \partial _{n} u_{2} + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } u_{2} - \epsilon \,\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 u_{2} &{}=g_{2}  &\text{ on }(\mathbb{R}_+^*\times \{0\}) \cap  V_{2} \\[1pt]
	\partial _{x} u_{2} &{}= 0 &\text{ on }(\{0\}\times \mathbb{R}_+^*) \cap  V_{2} \text{ and } \text{at }  (0,0)
\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
In~particular, we used the value of $\tilde{\rho}_{N\mkern-2mu,\mkern1mu\epsilon} f $ on $\partial \Omega^\circ$, as it gives $\partial _{n} u_{2|(\mathbb{R}_+^*)^2 } = \partial _{n} u_{1|\partial \Omega^\circ} \circ f ^{-1}$ and $\partial _{x} ^2 u_{2|\mathbb{R}_+^*\times \{0\}} = \partial _{x} ^2 u_{1|\Gamma^\circ} \circ f ^{-1}$. Let $b,c>0$ be s.t.\ $(b,0)=f (\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{3a}{5} ,0)$ and $(c,0)=f (\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{4a}{5} ,0)$. Let $\eta '>0$ be s.t.\ $[0,c]\times [0,\eta ']\subset V_{2}$. We extend $u_{2}$, $f_{2}$ and $g_{2}$ to $(-a',c)\times (0,\eta ')$ by setting:
\[\forall (x,y)\in (-c,0)\times (0,\eta '), \quad  u_{2} (x,y):=u_{2} (-x,y),\ f_{2} (x,y):=f_{2} (-x,y) \ \text{ and } \ g_{2} (x):=g_{2} (-x).\]
Thanks to \cref{regularite elliptique pour ME 2 preuve u2}, these extensions satisfy
\[\left\{\begin{array}{@{\,}r@{}l@{\;}l}
	\operatorname{div}(A \nabla  u_{2} ) &{}= f_{2} &\text{ in }R := (-c,c)\times (0,\eta ') \\[1pt]
	\mu _{0} \partial _{n} u_{2} + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon } u_{2} - \epsilon \,\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 u_{2} &{}=g_{2}  &\text{ on }I_{0} := (-c,c)\times \{0\}
\end{array}\right.\]
Moreover $A$ is Lipschitz because $Df $ is Lipschitz by \cref{diffeo ME}. A second application of \cref{regularite elliptique pour ME} yields $\|u_{2} \|_{H^{1/2} ((0,b)\times \{0\})} \leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon \,\big(\|f_{2} \|_{L^2 (R)} + \|g_{2} \|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )} +\|u_{2} \|_{H^{1} (R)} +\sqrt{\epsilon } \, \|u_{2} \|_{H^{1} (I_{0} )} \big)$. Thus:
\begin{align*}
	\|u\|_{H^{1/2} ((\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{3a}{5} )\times \{0\})} &\leqslant  \|u_{1} \|_{H^{1/2} ((\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{3a}{5} )\times \{0\})} + C |h(P^\circ)|\\
	&\leqslant  C \.\|u_{2} \|_{H^{1/2} ((0,b)\times \{0\})} + C |h(P^\circ)|\\
	&\leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon \,\big(\|f_{1} \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} + \|g_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} )} +\|u_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} +\sqrt{\epsilon } \.\snh{u_{1} }(\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} ) \big) \\
	& \quad  + C \.|h(P^\circ)| \\
	&\leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon \,\big(\|f\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)} + \|g\|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ)} +\|h\|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ)} +\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)} +\sqrt{\epsilon } \.\lvertu\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \big) \\
	& \quad + C_{M} \.|h(P^\circ)| 
\end{align*}
where we used in the last inequality:
\begin{itemize}
	\item $\|f_{1} \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} \leqslant  \|f\|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} + C\.\|h\|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$,
	\item $\|g_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} )} \leqslant \| \tilde{g} \|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} )} + C\.|\partial _{\theta } h(P^\circ)|+ \frac{C}{\epsilon } |h(P^\circ)|$ with $|\partial _{\theta } h(P^\circ)|\leqslant C \.\|h\|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$,
	\item $\|u_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} \leqslant  \|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ \cap V_{1} )} + C\.\|h\|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$,
	\item $\snh{u_{1} }(\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} ) \leqslant  \snh{u}(\Gamma^\circ \cap V_{1} ) + C\.|h(P^\circ)|$ with $|h(P^\circ)|\leqslant C \.\|h\|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ)}$. 
\end{itemize}
Finally we use $\|u\|_{H^{1/2} (\Gamma^\circ)} \leqslant  \|u\|_{H^{1/2} ((\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{3a}{5} )\times \{0\})} + \|u\|_{H^{1/2} ((\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}+ \frac{2a}{5} ,\infty )\times \{0\})}$.\medskip\smallskip
\endgroup                   

\underline{Step 2:\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex\vrule width 0pt depth 0.25ex} Let $\Omega^\circ_{1} ,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}_{1} ,\Sigma^\circ_{1} ,P^\circ_{1}$ be the values taken by $\Omega^\circ,\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ},\Sigma^\circ,P^\circ$ when $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}=1$. We assume $\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \in (0,R]$ and $\epsilon  \in (0,M\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}]$. We define the rescaled function $u_{1} :x\in \Omega^\circ_{1} \mapsto u(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} x)$ and similarly $g_{1} :=\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} g(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\vcenter{\hbox{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}} \.)$ and $h_{1} :=\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \.h(\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\vcenter{\hbox{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}} \.)$. Let $\epsilon _{1} :=\epsilon /\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}$. We have
\[\left\{\begin{array}{r@{}ll}
	\mu _{0} \Delta u_{1} &{}= f_{1} :=-\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^2  \omega ^2 \rho _{0} u_{1} &\text{ in }\Omega^\circ_{1} \\
	\mu _{0} \partial _{n} u_{1} + \frac{\mu _{1} }{\epsilon _{1}} u_{1} - \epsilon _{1} \,(\mu _{1} \partial _{x} ^2 +\omega ^2 \rho _{1} )u_{1} &{}=g_{1} &\text{ on }\Gamma^\circ_{1} \\
	\partial _{r} u_{1} &{}= h_{1} &\text{ on }\Sigma^\circ_{1} \text{ and } \text{at }  P^\circ_{1}
\end{array}\right.\]
Note that the boundary condition involves $\epsilon _{1}$ instead of $\epsilon $. Step 1 shows
\begin{multline*}
	\quad  \|u_{1} \|_{H^{1/2} (\Gamma^\circ_{1} )} \leqslant  C_{M} \,\epsilon _{1} \Big(\|f_{1} \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ_{1} )} + \|g_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Gamma^\circ_{1} )} +\|h_{1} \|_{H^2 (\Sigma^\circ_{1} )} \\
	+\|u_{1} \|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ_{1} )} +\sqrt{\epsilon _{1}} \, \snh{u_{1} }(\Gamma^\circ_{1} ) \Big) + C_{M} \.|h_{1} (P^\circ_{1} )|. \quad 
\end{multline*}
Moreover, for any $\psi :\Omega^\circ\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ regular enough, $\psi _{1} :=\psi (\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}\.\vcenter{\hbox{\scalebox{0.4}{$\bullet$}}} \.)$ and $j\in \mathbb{N}$, we have $\|\psi _{1} \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ_{1} )} = \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}^{-1} \|\psi \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)}$, $\|\nabla  \psi _{1} \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ_{1} )} = \|\nabla  \psi \|_{L^2 (\Omega^\circ)}$ and $\snh{\psi _{1} }(\Gamma^\circ_{1} ) = \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \.\lvert\psi \rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)}$. Thus, by~definition of $H_{\rm sc}^{j}$ in \cref{def: sobolev pondere pour ME}, we finally have:
\begin{multline*}
	\quad  \frac{\|u\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1/2}(\Gamma^\circ)}}{\sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}} \leqslant  C_{R,M} \frac{\epsilon }{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \bigg( \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\|g\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{1}(\Gamma^\circ)} + \sqrt{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}} \,\|h\|_{H_{\rm sc}^{2}(\Sigma^\circ)} \\
	+ \frac{\|u\|_{H^{1} (\Omega^\circ)}}{\@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ}}  +\sqrt{\epsilon } \,\lvertu\rvert_{\dot{H}^1(\Gamma^\circ)} \bigg) + C_{M} \@ifnextchar^{(R^\circ)}{R^\circ} \.|h(P^\circ)|. \quad 
\end{multline*}
